screening_results.reason: This study used FDG-PET with voxelwise SPM analyses comparing a clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patient group (n=10) against healthy controls (n=46). The methods describe Lund and Manchester clinical criteria emphasizing behavioral/frontal dysfunction, consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD). All inclusion requirements are met: imaging modality = FDG-PET (I3); patient sample comprises clinically diagnosed FTD likely representing bvFTD per criteria (I4); patient group size ≥6 (n=10) and control group ≥6 (n=46) (I5); reports direct group-level FTD versus healthy control contrasts (I6); the FTD group is analyzed separately from FTD-MND (I7); and voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses are reported (I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Although the paper doesn’t explicitly label the group as “bvFTD” in the excerpt, the diagnostic criteria and described behavioral/frontal features support classification as bvFTD for inclusion. If absolute certainty about explicit bvFTD labeling or coordinate tables is required, this can be checked during annotation, but it should be retained for screening.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. It used MRI and SPECT imaging rather than the required modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) (I3 not met). There is no group-level direct comparison of a bvFTD patient group against a healthy control group reported (I6 not met), and the patient sample is reported as clinically diagnosed FTD without a clearly defined bvFTD-only group compared directly to controls (I4 and I7 not met). The paper reports a clinical case series/cohort without a recruited control group; thus it meets exclusion criterion E11 (case series without control group). The study does meet the sample size criterion for the patient group (I5 met: 72 patients). Whole-brain stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD-vs-control contrast are not reported (I8 not met). Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis: (I3) Imaging modality is voxel-based morphometry (VBM) using SPM99. (I4) The paper includes a clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia (FTD) group defined by Neary criteria; the FTD patients are described by behavioral disturbances consistent with behavioral-variant FTD. (I5) Sample sizes meet thresholds: FTD (N=8) and controls (N=20), both ≥6. (I6) The paper reports group-level VBM contrasts directly comparing the FTD group against healthy controls (FTD vs controls). (I7) The FTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled with SemD) and compared with controls. (I8) Whole-brain VBM results are reported and localized (figures/tables referenced, corrected and uncorrected thresholds reported); localization to stereotactic atlases is described, indicating whole-brain stereotactic reporting. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore I include this study for the review.

This study uses task-based fMRI in a group of patients diagnosed with FTD (n=7) and compares them to an Alzheimer’s disease (AD) patient group (n=7). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI used), I5 (patient group size ≥6), I8 (paper reports stereotactic coordinates/Talairach coordinates in supplement). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (paper does not explicitly state patients are behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease—diagnosis given as FTD using Lund-Manchester criteria but bvFTD is not specified), I6 (no group-level comparison of bvFTD versus healthy control group; the comparator is an AD patient group), I7 (no bvFTD-versus-control contrast is reported, so sample-purity condition for that comparison cannot be satisfied). No exclusion criteria from the provided list (E5–E11) are directly applicable. Because key inclusion criteria (I4 and I6) are not met, the study is excluded.

This study uses FDG-PET and reports voxel-based, group-level comparisons between 29 clinically diagnosed FTD patients and age-matched controls with whole-brain voxel results (MNI coordinates provided). However, the patient sample is not pure bvFTD: three patients had mild associated signs of motor neuron disease (FTD-ALS/MND) and were included in the single pooled FTD group rather than analyzed separately. This violates inclusion criterion I7 (sample purity). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore exclude because I7 is not satisfied, although I3, I4, I5, I6, and I8 are met.

This article is a narrative/review and perspective on validating FDG-PET for frontotemporal dementia and proposes a pilot multicenter study, but does not present original empirical group-level FDG-PET data comparing a bvFTD (or Pick's disease) patient group to a healthy control group. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (non-empirical paper without original data). Inclusion criteria: I3 (uses FDG-PET) is satisfied. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (does not include a clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick patient sample), I5 (no patient/sample sizes reported ≥6), I6 (no group-level bvFTD vs healthy control contrast reported), I7 (no bvFTD-only group compared to controls), I8 (no whole-brain stereotactic coordinates reported). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Although the study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and included a sufficient sample size (FTD n=29; controls n=12) and included FTD patients with a subgroup described as having social/executive dysfunction (likely bvFTD), it does not report a group-level comparison of a bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) group separately against healthy controls. The FTD analyses are presented on a combined FTD group (including primary progressive aphasia subtypes and social/executive disorder) rather than an isolated bvFTD vs control contrast. Therefore key inclusion criteria I6 (direct bvFTD vs control group comparison) and I7 (bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups) are not met. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses voxel‐based morphometry (VBM) with SPM99 (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed FTD subgroups, including a non‐aphasic/behavioural subgroup (NON‑APH; n=14) consistent with bvFTD clinical presentation (I4). The NON‑APH subgroup sample size (n=14) and the healthy control imaging group (n=12) meet the minimum sample requirements (I5). The paper reports group‑level, whole‑brain voxelwise atrophy comparisons of FTD subgroups (including NON‑APH) versus healthy seniors (bvFTD/non‑aphasic subgroup < controls) (I6), and these subgroup versus control contrasts are not pooled with other patient groups (I7). The imaging results are reported after normalization to Talairach space and peak coordinates are referenced in tables/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria from the review are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This VBM study includes an FTD patient group but does not specify that patients had the behavioral variant (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I5 (FTD patient group n=8 and controls n=26 meet sample size), I6 (group-level patient(s) vs controls contrasts were performed), I7 (FTD group reported separately, not pooled with other patient groups), I8 (voxel-wise SPM results and at least one stereotactic coordinate reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (sample must be clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease) — the paper only reports FTD type without specifying bvFTD. No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for not meeting I4.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it used 18F-FDG PET (I3), included a clinical FTD patient group consistent with behavioral-variant FTD presentation (patients were diagnosed with FTD and primary progressive aphasia cases were excluded) (I4), had adequate sample sizes (25 FTD patients; 15 controls) (I5), reported a group-level voxelwise comparison of the FTD group versus healthy controls using SPM (two-sample t-test) (I6), did not pool the FTD group with other patient groups (SD reported separately) (I7), and reported stereotactic coordinates for peaks of hypometabolism (x/y/z maxima in Talairach space) (I8). Full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria from the review are met.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria required for this review. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I5 (patient group size >=6; FTLD n=14), and I8 (whole-brain voxel-wise SPM results reported with stereotactic coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no group-level comparison of bvFTD vs healthy controls — the main comparison is FTLD vs early-onset AD), and I7 (the FTLD patient group pools different clinical subtypes: FTD, semantic dementia, and PPA, so there is no pure bvFTD-only vs control contrast). I4 (explicit bvFTD/pick’s diagnosis) is not clearly satisfied because the paper reports “FTD” as part of a mixed FTLD group but does not report a separate bvFTD group compared directly to controls. No exclusion criteria from the provided list (E5–E11) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded for failing required inclusion criteria (I6, I7, and unclear I4).

Full text appears to be an abstract of a behavioral study assessing recognition of "humanness" in FTD patients. It does not report use of VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET as the primary imaging modality, nor any group-level voxelwise imaging analyses directly comparing a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD patient group to healthy controls with stereotactic coordinates. The sample description is FTD patients (n=16) split into right- and left-predominant groups, but the paper does not specify clinically-diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick disease, nor the presence/size of a healthy control imaging group required for the review. Because the provided content is limited to an abstract, core methodological and imaging results are missing (fulltext_incomplete). Therefore the study does not meet the required imaging and contrast inclusion criteria and is excluded.

This is an empirical VBM study directly comparing clinically-diagnosed frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patients with healthy controls. The authors selected a behavioral FTD phenotype (excluded progressive aphasia and semantic dementia) and describe core behavioral features consistent with bvFTD. Imaging modality: whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with voxel-by-voxel case–control comparisons. Sample sizes meet thresholds (9 FTD patients, 26 controls). A direct group-level contrast between the patient group and controls is reported (AnCova VBM results). The sample is not pooled with other patient groups; non-bvFTD variants were excluded. Stereotactic reporting is present (e.g., coordinates given for the periaqueductal gray and whole-brain VBM clusters are described), and the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be included for this review focused on bvFTD VBM studies.

This study reports voxel-wise FDG-PET comparisons between frontal-variant FTLD patients (fv-FTLD, equivalent to bvFTD) and healthy controls, with group-level SPM analyses and reported MNI coordinates. Sample sizes meet thresholds (18 patients, 24 controls). The paper includes direct bvFTD/controls contrasts (whole group and subgroups) and uses whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Full-text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied (see list). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and included 18 FTD patients and 17 controls (I3 and I5 satisfied). The cohort explicitly included cases with frontal-variant/frontotemporal behavioural features (fvFTD), so participants with bvFTD-like presentations were present (I4 satisfied). However, the paper does not report a group-level comparison that directly contrasts a bvFTD (or fvFTD-only) patient group against healthy controls; instead the authors analysed a mixed FTD group (SD and fvFTD) versus controls and reported covariate correlations. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 (direct bvFTD vs control group comparison) and I7 (bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups) are not met. I8 (coordinates for a bvFTD-vs-control contrast) is consequently not met. Full text appears complete. Excluded on these grounds.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses FDG-PET with voxel-wise SPM analysis (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed FTD patient group consistent with the Neary consensus criteria (corresponding to behavioral-variant FTD; I4), and has adequate sample sizes (29 patients, 11 healthy controls; I5). It reports group-level voxel-wise comparisons of the patient group versus healthy controls (I6) and the bvFTD/FTD group is not pooled with other patient subtypes (PNFA, semantic dementia, FTD+MND were excluded from the analyzed sample), satisfying sample purity (I7). Whole-brain stereotactic coordinates are reported and local maxima converted to Talairach space (I8). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore include.

Imaging modality and reporting: FDG-PET was used (I3 met), sample sizes meet thresholds (8 and 29 patients; controls n=11) (I5 met), and whole-brain SPM results with stereotactic coordinates are reported/mentioned (I8 met). However, the paper reports analyses for ‘FTD’ (frontotemporal dementia) as a whole and does not explicitly specify a cohort of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease patients, nor does it present a bvFTD-versus-control group-level comparison. Therefore I4 (bvFTD sample) and I6 (direct bvFTD vs control contrast) are not satisfied. I7 (sample purity: bvFTD not pooled with other subtypes) is also not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) are triggered. Because the review specifically requires bvFTD (or Pick’s) group-level contrasts versus controls, this study must be excluded.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and performed group-level VBM comparisons of pathologically defined subgroups (including Pick disease, PiD) against healthy controls. The PiD subgroup has n=7 (>=6) and controls n=20 (>=6). PiD was analyzed as a separate subgroup (not pooled), and direct patient-versus-control contrasts are reported. The paper describes whole-brain VBM analyses (regions/tables and figures of atrophy patterns), indicating whole-brain results in stereotactic space. The full text provided contains background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for imaging modality (I3), sample (I4), sample size (I5), contrast (I6), sample purity (I7), and reporting of whole-brain VBM results (I8). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a clinical series of 29 early FTD patients assessed with SPECT and PET but it does not report a group-level direct comparison between a bvFTD patient group and a healthy control group. It therefore fails inclusion criterion I6 (no bvFTD-versus-control group analysis). The imaging modality is SPECT and unspecified PET (not confirmed as FDG-PET), so I3 (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) is not met. The paper reports an FTD patient sample (29), satisfying the sample size requirement I5, but it does not explicitly specify clinically diagnosed bvFTD vs other FTD subtypes (I4 ambiguous) and does not report stereotactic whole-brain coordinates in the provided text (I8 not met). Because it is a case series without a recruited healthy control group, it meets exclusion criterion E11. Full text appears incomplete (abstract-level), limiting certainty.

This study used structural hippocampal volumetry and a visual MTA rating on MRI (ROI-based measures), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; therefore it does not meet the required imaging modality (I3). The analyses are ROI-only (hippocampal volumetry/MTA) with no whole-brain voxelwise results reported, so it meets exclusion criterion E6. Additionally, the paper does not report whole-brain stereotactic coordinates for a voxelwise bvFTD-vs-control comparison (I8 not met). Included: the study contains a separate FTD subgroup (likely behavioral-variant FTD) compared with controls (I4), has adequate sample sizes (FTD n=17; controls n=73) (I5), performs direct group-level patient vs control comparisons (I6), and the bvFTD/FTD group is reported separately (I7). However, failure to use an eligible imaging modality and the ROI-only focus (E6) are decisive exclusions for this review.

This study used FDG-PET and a large sample of clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD patients (N=70), and the patient group was not pooled with other dementia syndromes. Thus I3 (FDG-PET), I4 (clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD — equivalent to bvFTD in older nomenclature), I5 (>=6 patients), and I7 (bvFTD group not pooled) are met. However, the main analyses are data-driven PCA within the patient group and the paper does not present a group-level whole-brain voxelwise comparison of bvFTD patients versus a healthy control group (no direct bvFTD vs controls contrast reported in the results), so I6 is not met. Accordingly, I8 (reporting whole-brain stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD-vs-control comparison) is also not met. No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Therefore the paper does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria and should be excluded.

This is a VBM study (I3) that used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry to compare pathologically confirmed frontotemporal dementia groups to healthy controls. All cases fulfilled consensus criteria for frontotemporal dementia (clinical FTD, consistent with bvFTD/frontal-variant) and the discussion explicitly refers to frontal-variant frontotemporal dementia, satisfying I4. Group sizes meet the minimum (11 FTLD-U, 7 FTLD-MND; 18 controls), satisfying I5. The paper reports direct group-level comparisons of patient groups versus controls (FTLD-U vs controls; FTLD-MND vs controls), satisfying I6. Patient groups were analyzed separately (not pooled), satisfying I7. Whole-brain VBM results are reported and described in stereotactic terms (regions and survival after correction); per screening rules this is treated as meeting the coordinate-reporting requirement (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, ROI-only, case report, or non-FDG PET, etc.). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This longitudinal study uses 18F-FDG-PET (meets I3) in a clinically diagnosed ‘frontal variant’ FTD group (equivalent to bvFTD; meets I4). It reports group-level voxelwise comparisons of 22 patients versus 15 healthy controls (meets I5 and I6), with the patient group defined solely as FTD (not pooled with other FTD subtypes; meets I7). Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported and maxima are given in Talairach space, indicating stereotactic coordinates were used (meets I8). No exclusion criteria are met: the tracer is FDG (E10 not applicable), analyses are whole-brain voxelwise rather than ROI-only (E6 not met), study is empirical with a control group (E8/E11 not met), and methods are appropriate (not seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness only, so E9 not met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Summary: This paper uses VBM and includes a clinically diagnosed FTD (behavioral-variant FTD) group (n=14) and healthy controls (n=20), and reports voxelwise MNI coordinates for correlations between regional atrophy and oculomotor measures. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (includes FTD patients), I5 (patient and control groups each >=6). However, the paper does not present a group-level voxelwise contrast that directly compares the bvFTD/FTD group against healthy controls (e.g., FTD < controls) in a whole-brain VBM or FDG-PET group comparison. Instead, the imaging results focus on correlations between brain volume and antisaccade performance across combined groups and VBM analyses that control for diagnostic group, and some analyses pool FTLD subtypes; no explicit FTD vs control voxelwise comparison with coordinates is reported in the supplied full text. Therefore the study fails I6 (direct bvFTD vs control group-level comparison) and I8 (reporting stereotactic coordinates for such a contrast). It also fails I7 insofar as there is no discrete bvFTD-versus-control imaging contrast (FTLD subtypes are sometimes combined). Conclusion: Excluded because required direct bvFTD vs healthy-control group-level imaging comparison (with coordinates) is not reported.

This study used FDG-PET and included eight FTD patients (meets I3 and I5). However, it does not specify enrollment of behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease specifically (I4 not met). Crucially, no group-level comparison between a bvFTD (or FTD) patient group and a healthy control group is reported—analyses are descriptive of the patient series rather than a patient-versus-control contrast (I6 not met). The bvFTD-versus-control comparison is therefore absent, sample purity for a bvFTD-only group is unconfirmed (I7 not met), and no whole-brain stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD>control or control>bvFTD contrast are provided (I8 not met). This is a small consecutive clinical series without a recruited control group, meeting exclusion criterion E11 (case series without a control group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Conclusion: EXCLUDE. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I6, I7, I8. Exclusion criteria met: E11.

This study uses whole-brain VBM (I3) and includes a separately reported frontotemporal dementia (FTD) variant group consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) with n=30 and healthy controls (n=20), so I4 and I5 are met. However, the paper explicitly states that normal controls were not used in any VBM analysis and does not present a direct group-level bvFTD-versus-healthy-control comparison (e.g., bvFTD < controls) as required by I6. Consequently there is no bvFTD-vs-control whole-brain contrast (so I7 and I8 are not satisfied). The paper reports VBM coordinates for its regression and subgroup interaction analyses, but these do not fulfill the specific requirement for a bvFTD>control or control>bvFTD whole-brain comparison. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to provide the required direct bvFTD vs. healthy control group-level comparison and associated whole-brain coordinates for that contrast.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis: it used 18F-FDG PET (I3); enrolled clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients and explicitly excluded semantic dementia and non-fluent progressive aphasia (consistent with a bvFTD sample) (I4); included adequate sample sizes (29 patients, 16 controls) (I5); reports a group-level voxelwise comparison of patients versus healthy controls (I6); the patient group was not pooled with other FTD subtypes (I7); and results are reported in stereotactic coordinates (Talairach/MNI) (I8). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, coordinates/clusters) is present. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the paper should be included for the review.

The study uses VBM (I3 met), includes clinically characterised FTD patients with prominent behavioural features consistent with bvFTD (I4 met), and has adequate sample sizes (16 patients, 9 controls) (I5 met). However, it does NOT present a group-level analysis that directly compares a bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) patient group against a healthy control group: the between-group contrast reported is FTLD (combined patient group) versus controls, and the other imaging analyses are within-FTLD regressions relating grey-matter to eating behaviours. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 (direct bvFTD-vs-control contrast) and I7 (bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups) are not satisfied. I8 (coordinates for a bvFTD-vs-control whole-brain contrast) is also not applicable/fulfilled because the required contrast is absent. No exclusion criteria from the review list are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because the key contrast required by the review (bvFTD vs controls, unpooled) is not reported.

Excluded because the paper does not present a group-level voxelwise comparison of a bvFTD-only patient group versus healthy controls; instead it compares PGRN(+) and PGRN(−) FTLD-U groups (each including mixed clinical phenotypes) to controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients among the sample), I5 (patient groups and control groups have ≥6 participants). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no direct group-level bvFTD vs healthy control contrast reported), I7 (bvFTD patients are pooled with other FTLD phenotypes in the reported patient-group vs control comparisons), I8 (no coordinates reported for a bvFTD-vs-control whole-brain contrast). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete.

This study uses FDG-PET and includes a clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD (fv-FTD) sample (13 patients) and control groups for behavioural testing; however, the imaging analyses reported are within-patient voxelwise correlations between FDG uptake and autobiographical memory measures rather than a group-level voxelwise comparison of bvFTD/fv-FTD patients versus healthy controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET imaging), I4 (clinically diagnosed fv-FTD, equivalent to bvFTD), I5 (>=6 patients in patient group), and I7 (patient group not pooled with other dementia syndromes). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no reported group-level bvFTD vs healthy control voxelwise comparison). I8 (coordinates for a bvFTD-vs-control contrast) is not applicable because such a contrast was not reported. No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the paper does not satisfy the required contrast criterion for inclusion in the meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD subjects (bvFTD) that reports group-level whole-brain VBM comparisons against matched healthy controls. Sample sizes meet the minimum (7 and 10 patients in subgroups; matched controls recruited), and the paper describes and reports voxelwise SPM analyses (whole-brain) comparing patient groups to controls. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study used VBM (I3) and both patient groups and controls meet the minimum sample-size criterion (FTLD-T n=6, FTLD-U n=8, controls n=61) (I5). However, the sample consists of pathologically-defined FTLD subtypes (FTLD-T and FTLD-U), not a clinically-diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease group. The paper does not present a direct group-level comparison of a bvFTD patient group versus healthy controls (I4 and I6 not met). Consequently, criteria I7 (sample purity of a bvFTD-vs-control comparison) and I8 (coordinates reported for a bvFTD-vs-control whole-brain comparison) are also not satisfied. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This study uses FDG-PET (meets I3) and includes sufficient sample sizes (14 FTD patients, 33 controls; meets I5). However it does NOT meet key inclusion requirements: (a) I4 — the patient group consists of pathologically-confirmed FTD cases and heterogeneous FTD subtypes rather than a clearly defined clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease cohort; (b) I6 — the paper does not present a group-level voxel-wise comparison directly contrasting a clinically-defined bvFTD patient group versus a recruited healthy control group (analyses are diagnostic/individual SSP comparisons and comparisons between FTD and AD, not a reported bvFTD>controls voxelwise group contrast); (c) I8 — no whole-brain stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) for a bvFTD-versus-control contrast are reported in the main text. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) are directly triggered by the full text provided. Because several required inclusion criteria are not met, the study must be excluded.

This study uses FDG-PET with voxel-wise, whole-brain SPM analyses comparing clinically diagnosed frontal/behavioral variant FTD patients against recruited healthy controls. The PET substudy includes 41 patients and 16 controls (both ≥6). Group-level contrasts directly compare patient groups versus healthy controls and report stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) for maxima. The bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient subtypes (only frontal/behavioral variant included). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion enabling assessment. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study uses VBM and reports a group-level voxel-wise comparison between a subgroup of patients clinically diagnosed with frontotemporal dementia (frontal/behavioral variant FTD; n=6 overeaters) and healthy controls (n=47). The imaging modality is VBM (I3). The patient subgroup consists of clinically diagnosed FTD patients consistent with the behavioral/frontal variant described in the text (I4). The patient group size meets the minimum (n=6) and controls exceed 6 (I5). A direct group contrast of the FTD overeaters versus controls is reported (I6), the FTD overeater group is not pooled with other patient groups (I7), and stereotactic coordinates for atrophied regions are provided (I8). Core article sections (methods, results, discussion) are present in the supplied full text.

This study is excluded because it does not perform a bvFTD (behavioral FTD) versus healthy control group comparison (fails I6). It instead compares patient subgroups (FTLD+UIC vs FTLD−UIC), and although it includes FTD patients, the primary analyses are within patient groups and there is no recruited healthy control group (meets exclusion E11). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET imaging used), I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients), I5 (patient group sizes >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no bvFTD vs healthy control group comparison), I7 (no bvFTD-versus-control comparison; patient groups are pooled across FTLD subtypes in main analyses), I8 (no whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control coordinates reported). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is excluded because it does not provide a group-level VBM/whole-brain imaging comparison of a clinically defined bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) or Pick disease group versus healthy controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses voxel-based morphometry / whole-brain structural MRI analyses). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the sample comprises a heterogeneous FTD spectrum and pathologically defined subgroups, but does not report a clinically defined bvFTD or Pick disease group explicitly), I5 (the imaging subgroup contrasts report very small patient subgroup sizes: tau-positive n=5, tau-negative n=4, fv-AD n=3, so patient groups for the imaging analyses do not meet the ≥6 participants requirement), I6 (no direct bvFTD-versus-control group-level comparison is reported), I7 (no pure bvFTD group versus controls — patient groups are pathologically defined and small), I8 (although imaging peak loci are summarized, there is no clear report of a bvFTD vs control whole-brain coordinate contrast). No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) are directly triggered by the manuscript content provided. Full text appears complete. Given these failures to meet multiple inclusion criteria, the paper must be excluded from the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not use an eligible imaging modality and reports only regional (lobar) volumetric ROI analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise results. Exclusion IDs met: E6 (reports only ROI/regional volumetric analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise coordinates). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD cases consistent with bvFTD/FTD), I5 (sample sizes: FTD n=12, controls n=24), I6 (reports group-level comparisons of FTD vs controls), I7 (FTD group is reported separately from semantic dementia). Inclusion IDs NOT met: I3 (does NOT use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — it uses structural volumetric segmentation), I8 (does NOT report whole-brain stereotactic coordinates/MNI or Talairach voxelwise results). Full text appears complete for screening purposes (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical VBM study that directly compares early-stage MSTD patients with bvFTD against age- and gender-matched healthy controls. The methods state use of optimized/modulated VBM (SPM2) and report group-level patient<control whole-brain comparisons (significant grey matter loss clusters, with stereotactic locations referenced in supplementary Table 4). The VBM sample included seven patients and 19 controls (≥6 each). The bvFTD group is not pooled with other diagnoses. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for the review are met.

This study is excluded because it does not use an eligible imaging modality and reports only ROI/lobar volumetry rather than whole-brain voxelwise results. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports only region-of-interest/lobar volume analyses with no whole-brain VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET results). The paper used voxel-based morphometry and included an FTLD patient group (N=18) and controls (N=40), so inclusion criteria I3 (VBM) and I5 (sample size) are met. However the FTLD group is reported as a pooled autopsy-proven FTLD sample without specification that participants had clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease; thus I4 (bvFTD/Pick's sample) is not met. The key contrast required (bvFTD versus healthy controls) is not demonstrated—the study reports FTLD versus controls rather than a bvFTD-only versus control comparison—so I6 (direct bvFTD vs control contrast) and I7 (bvFTD group not pooled with other patient subtypes) are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) appear to apply. Full text appears incomplete here (only abstract/metadata provided), so fulltext_incomplete=true. Therefore EXCLUDED.

The study uses SPECT (99mTc-ECD) perfusion imaging, whereas the review inclusion I3 requires VBM, fMRI (resting/task), or FDG-PET. Although the study meets multiple other inclusion criteria — I4 (includes clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD/fvFTD), I5 (patient group n=48 and control group n=15), I6 (reports group-level comparisons of fvFTD and other patient subgroups vs controls), I7 (bvFTD/fvFTD reported separately, not pooled), and I8 (whole-brain SPM analyses with stereotactic coordinates reported) — it fails I3 (imaging modality). No exclusion criteria from the provided list (E5–E11) are directly met. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it does not use an eligible imaging modality for this review.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports whole-brain voxelwise comparisons of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient groups versus a recruited healthy control group (each bvFTD subgroup n=15; controls n=45), satisfying sample size requirements. Group-level contrasts (each bvFTD stage vs controls) are explicitly reported with whole-brain correction and region results (eTable/figures). Although some bvFTD participants had coexisting motor neuron disease (MND), the authors performed sensitivity analyses excluding MND cases and found core results unchanged, supporting sample purity for the bvFTD-versus-control comparisons. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is a multicenter empirical FDG-PET study that includes a separately reported frontal-variant FTD group (interpretable as bvFTD), with large sample sizes (FTD n=98; controls n=110). The paper uses 18F-FDG PET (I3), reports clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD patients (I4), and meets sample-size requirements (I5). It performs group-level voxel-based comparisons of the patient groups versus a recruited healthy control group using spatial normalization to Talairach space and voxelwise Z maps/3D-SSP (satisfying I6 and I8). The FTD (frontal-variant) group is analyzed separately rather than pooled with other patient groups (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not a review, uses FDG tracer, includes whole-brain voxelwise analyses rather than ROI-only, and is an empirical study with an adequate control group). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria and is included.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the required imaging-modality and whole-brain coordinate reporting criteria. Exclusion IDs met: E6 (study reports regional/ROI volumetric analyses using the SABRE ROI system and multivariate PLS rather than whole-brain voxelwise analyses with stereotactic coordinates). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes an FTD subgroup consistent with behavioral-variant FTD), I5 (sample sizes: FTD subgroup n=8 and scanning control group n=10 meet the >=6 requirement), I6 (group-level comparisons between patient subgroups, including FTD, and a matched scanning control group were reported), I7 (patient subgroups are reported separately, not pooled). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (required imaging modality: VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — this study used structural regional volumetry, not an accepted modality), I8 (no whole-brain voxelwise stereotactic coordinate results reported). This study uses voxel-based MRI analysis and includes a frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patient group (n=12) and matched controls (n=12), but it does not present a group-level comparison of a bvFTD-only cohort versus healthy controls. The FTD group is pooled (contains behavioral, language, and corticobasal presentations) and the paper reports FTD vs controls rather than a bvFTD-specific contrast. Therefore it fails the sample-purity and contrast requirements for inclusion in a bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

Although this study used VBM (I3) and included clinically diagnosed FTD patients (behavioral-variant FTD subgroup, n=15) with adequate sample sizes (controls and patient groups ≥6) satisfying I4 and I5, it does NOT report a group-level VBM contrast that directly compares a bvFTD (FTD) group alone versus healthy controls. The VBM results and tissue-loss contrasts are reported for FTLD as a combined group (FTD + SD) versus controls, and physiological correlations were performed with the combined FTLD group. Therefore criteria I6 (direct bvFTD-vs-control group comparison) and I7 (bvFTD group not pooled in that comparison) are not met. I8 (coordinates for a bvFTD-vs-control whole-brain contrast) is consequently not satisfied. No exclusion criteria from the review list apply. Hence the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on bvFTD vs controls VBM contrasts.

This study meets all inclusion requirements for the bvFTD-focused review. Imaging modality: used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) of MRI and FDG-PET (I3). Sample: clinically diagnosed FTD patients selected using consensus criteria, with explicit exclusion of semantic dementia and progressive nonfluent aphasia—i.e., the sample corresponds to behavioural-variant FTD rather than language variants (I4). Sample size: 13 FTD patients and 20 healthy controls (both groups >6) (I5). Contrast: reports voxel-wise group-level comparisons between FTD and healthy controls (e.g., NC > FTD) using SPM (I6). Sample purity: FTD group was not pooled with other patient groups (SD/PNFA were excluded) (I7). Coordinates/whole-brain results: the paper describes whole-brain SPM voxel-wise analyses in stereotactic space and reports tables/figures of results (I8). No exclusion criteria appear to be met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; tables of coordinates are referenced. Consequently, I include this study for the review.

The study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients with a behavioral (bvFTD-like) subgroup; it also includes a healthy control group. However, the group-level patient-versus-control comparison reported in the paper is performed on the entire FTD sample pooled (behavioral + aphasic presentations) rather than on a bvFTD (behavioral) group alone. Therefore the paper does not report a direct bvFTD-versus-healthy-control whole-brain contrast (in stereotactic space) as required. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM), I4 (includes bvFTD patients in sample), I5 (sample sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no bvFTD-specific vs control group-level comparison), I7 (sample purity violated because FTD group pooled), I8 (no bvFTD-vs-control coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD group (FTD-fv), which corresponds to bvFTD (I4); has adequate sample sizes (25 FTD-fv patients, 14 healthy controls) (I5); reports group-level whole-brain VBM comparisons directly contrasting the FTD-fv group against healthy controls (I6); the FTD-fv group was analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups) (I7); and the paper reports stereotactic coordinates (MNI) for whole-brain results (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results (including coordinates), and discussion, so fulltext appears complete.

This study reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing behavioural-variant FTD participants to healthy controls, with results reported in stereotactic (MNI) coordinates and tables. Sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases (N=26 overall; imaging subset N=21) and controls (N=16 overall; imaging subset N=12), meeting minimum sample size. Group-level contrasts directly compare bvFTD (FTDp subgroup) versus controls and report regional atrophy (with MNI coordinates in Table 2). The paper does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/coordinates referenced) is present and sufficient for screening.

This study is excluded because it does not provide a direct bvFTD-versus-healthy-control group-level comparison as required. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET), I4 (the sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD patients among the FTLD cohort), I5 (patient and control group sizes exceed 6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no group-level analysis directly comparing a bvFTD-only group against healthy controls; reported comparisons are for combined FTLD versus controls and FTLD subgroups but not bvFTD-alone versus controls), I7 (the bvFTD cases are pooled within a broader FTLD group rather than reported as a separate bvFTD group compared with controls), I8 (there is no bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain coordinate table reported because the specific bvFTD-vs-control contrast was not performed). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered by the provided full text. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This study used voxel-based morphometry (optimized VBM) and whole-brain analyses (Methods) and reports contrasts against a healthy control group. The cohort includes a SOC/EXEC subgroup (n=26) that corresponds to the behavioral/social/executive clinical phenotype (i.e., behavioral-variant FTLD/bvFTD), and 27 healthy controls—meeting the >=6 subjects requirement. The paper reports group-level VBM contrasts of patient subgroups versus controls and whole-brain masked regression results; results are summarized in tables and figures (Tables 3–4, Figures 1–2), indicating reported anatomic findings in stereotactic terms. Although the paper uses the SOC/EXEC terminology rather than the explicit label “bvFTD,” this subgroup corresponds to behavioral-variant FTD. Minor uncertainty remains because the excerpt does not explicitly state “bvFTD” or show numeric stereotactic coordinates, but the full paper presents whole-brain VBM contrasts vs controls and anatomical tables. Inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=31) and a healthy control group (n=56), and reports whole-brain voxelwise comparisons of bvFTD patients versus controls (regions of GM atrophy in all bvFTD patients compared with controls are described and shown). The paper uses SPM VBM methods and reports results in standard stereotactic space (methods and supplementary Table S2 referenced). All required inclusion criteria are met (VBM modality, bvFTD sample, adequate sample sizes, direct group-level bvFTD vs control contrast, bvFTD group analyzed separately, and whole-brain stereotactic results reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion provided. Inclusion criteria applied: ["I3","I4","I5","I6","I7","I8"]. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) group of 51 patients (I4, I5), and a healthy control group of 14 subjects (I5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain patient-versus-control comparisons (two-sample t tests comparing each patient group to controls) (I6) and the bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups) (I7). The methods and results describe whole-brain SPM5 analyses with multiple-comparisons corrections and refer to reported clusters/tables (table e-1 and figures), indicating whole-brain stereotactic results were reported (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (exclusion_criteria_applied: []). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion); supplemental coordinates are referenced. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the bvFTD meta-analysis.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports group-level, whole-brain comparisons of mutation carriers with bvFTD diagnoses against cognitively normal controls. The methods state a VBM analysis and that analyses were repeated assessing only subjects with a clinical diagnosis of bvFTD (n=7 PGRN, n=11 MAPT), with reported results (fig e-1) indicating direct patient-versus-control contrasts. Patient subgroup sizes meet the >=6 requirement. The bvFTD subgroup comparisons are not pooled with other diagnostic groups. Whole-brain VBM results are described and presented (figures/tables and supplemental material referenced), meeting the coordinate-reporting criterion per instructions to judge the full paper. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, uses VBM, not a case report). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clearly defined subgroup of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and reports group-level voxelwise comparisons against healthy controls. Methods state use of voxel-based morphometry with whole-brain voxelwise analyses corrected for multiple comparisons (FWE/FDR) and figures/slices showing results. The bvFTD-specific analyses were performed on subjects with a clinical diagnosis of bvFTD (n=15 tau-positive and n=30 TDP-43-positive, and pooled bvFTD severity groups), each compared to age- and gender-matched controls, satisfying sample size requirements (>6 per group) and sample purity (bvFTD analyzed separately, not pooled with other diagnoses). The paper describes whole-brain stereotactic voxelwise results (voxel-based morphometry, corrected p-values, and image displays), meeting the coordinate/reporting requirement. No exclusion criteria were met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=11) alongside healthy controls (n=8) (I4, I5). The paper reports group-level VBM analyses comparing disease groups and explicitly reports results for bvFTD versus controls (e.g. bvFTD minus controls—lateral orbitofrontal gyrus, BA10, p=0.000, cluster=2,478), satisfying the requirement for a direct patient-versus-control contrast (I6). The diagnostic groups were analysed separately (bvFTD not pooled with other patient groups), meeting sample purity (I7). The methods state VBM analyses with small-volume corrections and reference to coordinates (Table 1) and report stereotactic loci/BA for clusters, indicating whole-brain stereotactic reporting (I8). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion; tables are referenced though some coordinate tables may be in tables/supplementary files. Overall, the study is eligible for inclusion in the bvFTD VBM meta-analysis.

Exclusion rationale: This study is excluded because it reports region-of-interest manual volumetry rather than whole-brain voxelwise analyses (meets exclusion E6). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (sample size: patient groups and controls both exceed 6; FTD n=12, controls n=27). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality requirement — study did not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; it used manual cortical parcellation/volumetry), I4 (sample must be clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Picks disease — the paper reports ‘FTD’ without explicit specification of behavioral-variant bvFTD), I6 (contrast must be bvFTD versus healthy controls — although an FTD vs control comparison is reported, it does not clearly identify a bvFTD group), I8 (requires whole-brain stereotactic coordinates for the patient-versus-control comparison — not provided because the study used ROI volumetry). This study used FDG-PET (I3) and included a clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD group (fv-FTD, corresponding to bvFTD; I4) with adequate sample sizes (18 patients, 18 controls; I5). Patient groups were reported separately (fv-FTD and SD), so the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups (I7). However, the paper does not report any group-level whole-brain comparison directly contrasting the bvFTD/fv-FTD group against healthy controls (e.g., bvFTD < controls); the PET analyses presented are correlations within patient groups between fluency scores and FDG uptake. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (required direct patient-versus-control group comparison) and I8 (reporting whole-brain coordinates for such a bvFTD-versus-control contrast). Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because key inclusion criteria I6 and I8 are not met.

This study directly addresses bvFTD using FDG-PET (with arterial sampling) and also reports voxel-based morphometry (SPM) whole-brain analyses. The sample comprises 24 clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD patients and 12 age-matched controls (both groups >6). The paper reports group-level comparisons of bvFTD subgroups versus healthy controls (repeated-measures ANOVAs, ROI PET contrasts) and voxel-based morphometry SPM comparisons (whole-brain) between patient groups and controls; coordinates are implied to be reported (supplementary information) and SPM maps/voxel extractions are described. The bvFTD group is not pooled with other dementia groups. No exclusion criteria apply (FDG tracer used; not a review; includes whole-brain analyses and control group). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8.

This study meets the review criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports whole-brain SPM analyses (I3, I8). The cohort includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and the authors explicitly re-categorized patients by clinical syndrome and contrasted bvFTD against 25 healthy controls (I4, I6, I7). The total patient sample is 18 and the study reports group-level parametric analyses for bvFTD (with corrected statistics), indicating the patient-group sample meets the minimum size requirement (I5). No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, ROI-only, inappropriate imaging modality, or case-series issues), and the provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the paper should be included for the bvFTD meta-analysis.

This study uses manual ROI volumetry of the putamen on T1 MRI (manual tracing), not VBM, task/resting‑state fMRI, or FDG‑PET, so it does not meet the required imaging-modality inclusion (I3). It reports only region-based volumetric analyses rather than whole‑brain voxelwise results in stereotactic space (violates E6 and fails I8). Met inclusion criteria: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed FTD diagnosed by Neary criteria, i.e., behavioral-variant FTD), I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6), I6 (reports group-level FTD vs control comparisons), and I7 (FTD group analyzed separately, not pooled). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Therefore the paper must be excluded from the review despite adequate sample size and group comparisons.

This study meets several inclusion criteria: it used voxel-based morphometry (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (I4), and the bvFTD and control groups each exceed the 6-participant threshold (I5). However, it does not report any group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrast that directly compares the bvFTD group against healthy controls (e.g., bvFTD < controls). The imaging analyses reported are correlation/voxelwise regression analyses across a mixed multi-diagnostic sample and co-atrophy/shared-effects checks; they controlled for diagnostic group membership but did not present a dedicated bvFTD-versus-control VBM comparison with stereotactic coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 (direct bvFTD vs control group-level comparison), I7 (that such a comparison be bvFTD alone, not pooled), and I8 (reporting whole-brain coordinates for that bvFTD-vs-control contrast) are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria from the provided list were triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM), includes a frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patient group (n=47) and healthy controls (n=43), reports whole-brain results in MNI space, and has adequate sample sizes. However, it does not report any group-level VBM contrast that directly compares a behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) group against healthy controls. The imaging analyses are correlational (personality trait–VBM regressions) across a mixed diagnostic sample, and while diagnostic-group covariates were used in co-atrophy checks, no bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast is presented and the bvFTD group is not isolated in an imaging contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (required direct bvFTD vs control group-level comparison) and I7 (bvFTD-versus-control comparison with bvFTD not pooled). No exclusion criteria from the list are met. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because its imaging data are structural ROI-based MRI volumetry (Freesurfer parcellation) rather than VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). It reports ROI volume comparisons (orbitofrontal, middle frontal gyrus) rather than whole-brain voxelwise results with stereotactic coordinates, so the coordinate requirement (I8) is not met and it falls under exclusion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (bvFTD patient sample), I5 (≥6 patients and ≥6 controls), I6 (group-level bvFTD vs control comparisons), I7 (bvFTD group not pooled with other diagnoses). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (required imaging modalities) and I8 (whole-brain stereotactic coordinates). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This FDG-PET study does not meet the review’s key population and contrast requirements. While it uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes an FTD patient group of sufficient size (n=17, I5), it does not report a group-level comparison of a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) group against a recruited healthy control group. The paper used an internal/normative PET database for individual case comparisons and reported PET-vs-clinical diagnostic accuracy within a consecutive patient series, but did not present a whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise group analysis or stereotactic coordinates. Therefore it fails I4 (bvFTD sample), I6 (bvFTD vs healthy control group-level contrast), I7 (cannot verify a pure bvFTD-vs-control comparison), and I8 (no whole-brain coordinates for such a contrast). Exclusion applied: E11 (clinical case series without a recruited control group/group-level patient-vs-control voxelwise analysis). Full text appears complete.

This paper reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses including a separate behavioral/dysexecutive (bvFTLD/bvFTD) subgroup (n=71) and compares cortical atrophy in that subgroup against an age-matched healthy control cohort (reported as ~42–43 controls) using independent-samples t tests. The methods state images were normalized into MNI space and the manuscript references tables of peak coordinates and whole-brain results (VBM, whole-brain analysis). All inclusion criteria are met: VBM imaging (I3); clinically diagnosed bvFTLD group present (I4); sufficient sample sizes for patient and control groups (I5); explicit group-level bvFTLD vs healthy control contrast (I6); bvFTLD group analyzed separately (I7); and whole-brain results in stereotactic space reported (I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports structural MRI regional volumetry (striatal and thalamic VOIs) comparing apathetic vs non-apathetic FTD patients, not a whole-brain VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET analysis. Inclusion criterion I5 (sample size ≥6 patients) is met (N=21). However, it fails key inclusion criteria: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no group-level bvFTD vs healthy control comparison; the reported contrasts are within FTD subgroups), and I4 (paper reports ‘FTD’ without specifying clinically diagnosed bvFTD group for a bvFTD-vs-control contrast). Additionally, the study reports ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results, meeting exclusion criterion E6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because although the study uses VBM (I3), includes a separate FTD patient group (11 FTD patients, likely bvFTD) (I4), and meets minimum sample sizes for patients and controls (I5), it does NOT report a group-level voxelwise comparison directly contrasting a bvFTD (FTD) patient group against healthy controls (fails I6). The paper’s VBM analyses relate atrophy to Flanker performance across a mixed diagnostic sample rather than presenting a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast, and no explicit whole-brain stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD vs control contrast are provided (fails I8). No exclusion criteria from E5–E11 apply.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=66) with an age- and gender-matched control group (n=30). The paper performs voxel-based morphometry group-level comparisons of bvFTD subgroups and bvFTD versus controls (whole-brain analyses reported and FWE-corrected results described). The sample is exclusively bvFTD (not pooled with other diagnostic groups) for the bvFTD vs control contrasts. The manuscript contains full methods, results and discussion (full text provided). Therefore it satisfies imaging modality (VBM), clinical sample, minimum sample sizes, group-level bvFTD-vs-control contrasts, sample purity, and reports whole-brain VBM results (coordinates/maps described).

This FDG-PET study meets several inclusion criteria for the review (modality FDG-PET; group-level voxelwise comparisons of patients vs controls; adequate sample sizes) but does not explicitly report a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease group. The patient group is described as ‘FTLD’ (frontotemporal lobar degeneration) without specification of clinical variant; inclusion criterion I4 (bvFTD or Pick’s disease) is therefore not satisfied. Because I4 is mandatory, the study must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET imaging), I5 (>=6 patients in patient group), I6 (direct group-level patient vs control comparisons), I8 (whole-brain voxelwise SPM analysis reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (bvFTD/Pick’s disease sample not specified), I7 (sample purity regarding a bvFTD-only group cannot be established). No exclusion criteria from the review list are triggered by the paper as supplied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (12 bvFTD patients) within the sample (I4); the bvFTD group size (n=12) and the control group (n=30) satisfy the minimum sample sizes (I5); the paper reports group-level VBM comparisons of patient groups versus healthy controls (bvFTD vs controls) (I6); the bvFTD group was analyzed separately rather than pooled with other patient groups (I7); and whole-brain VBM analyses were performed using SPM5 with normalization to standard space (MNI) and reported voxelwise results, fulfilling the coordinates/whole-brain reporting requirement (I8). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

The paper uses VBM and includes a separate behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) cohort (n=10) and a healthy control group (n=10). The Methods and Results describe group-level whole-brain VBM contrasts of each disease cohort versus controls, including bvFTD versus controls (with VBM outputs reported). Although coordinate tables are not visible in the excerpt, the paper explicitly reports whole-brain VBM comparisons; per screening instructions this is sufficient. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses VBM (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4). The paper reports group-level VBM comparisons of the clinical bvFTD subgroup against healthy controls (I6), the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups in that comparison (I7), and whole-brain results are reported from VBM (I8). However, it fails inclusion criterion I5 because the bvFTD patient subgroup is very small (n=3 in the atypical AD subgroup and n=3 in the FTLD subgroup), below the required minimum of 6 patients for the bvFTD group. Therefore the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

The study uses FDG-PET and reports voxel-wise group comparisons of FTD patients (n=13) vs controls (meets I3, I5, I6, I7, and I8). However, the patient group is described as ‘fronto-temporal dementia (FTD)’ without specifying the behavioral variant (bvFTD) or Pick's disease. Inclusion criterion I4 requires clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick's disease specifically. Because the paper does not specify that the FTD group is bvFTD (and cannot be assumed), it fails I4 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not report a group-level imaging contrast directly comparing a bvFTD-only patient group against healthy controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses voxel-based morphometry and task fMRI), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (bvFTD n=10 and controls n>=6). Although the study uses whole-brain VBM (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients among its cohort (I4) and has sufficient sample sizes (42 patients, 30 controls) satisfying the >=6 requirement (I5), it does NOT report any group-level analysis that directly compares a clinically defined bvFTD patient group against healthy controls. This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) (I4) and a healthy control group (n=21) with both groups >=6 participants (I5); it reports group-level comparisons that directly contrast diagnostic groups including bvFTD versus controls (ANOVA and post-hoc tests showing NC > bvFTD in right parietal lobe) (I6); the bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled) (I7); and the paper describes whole-brain VBM analyses in stereotactic space with voxelwise results (I8). The study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (n=10) (I4) with an adequate sample size and a healthy control group (n=20) (I5). This study examines frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) as a group (14 FTLD patients) rather than explicitly and specifically recruiting/labeling behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease. This empirical study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare multiple bvFTD patient groups (C9ORF72, MAPT, GRN, and sporadic bvFTD) against a recruited healthy control group (n=40). This study uses structural MRI volumetrics (BSI, FreeSurfer regional volumes) and nonlinear intra-subject fluid registrations, not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET — so it fails inclusion criterion I3 (required imaging modalities). The paper does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases (I4), has sufficient sample size (6 patients with longitudinal MRI, 15 controls) (I5), presents group-level patient vs healthy control comparisons of volumetric measures (I6), and the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups (I7). Therefore the study must be excluded.
