The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore I include this paper for the review.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used VBM (voxel-based morphometry) alongside DTI (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=27) (I4) with healthy controls (n=20) and AD patients (I5) satisfying the minimum group sizes, reports group-level contrasts directly comparing bvFTD versus healthy controls (I6), the bvFTD group is reported separately rather than pooled with other patient groups (I7), and VBM results are described and reported in standard/MNI space with whole-brain analyses (I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) apply: this is an original empirical study with whole-brain VBM results (not ROI-only), not a review, not an excluded imaging modality, and not a case report. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

This study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports group-level contrasts comparing a separate behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) patient group (n=10) against healthy controls (n=14). Sample sizes meet the >=6 requirement for both patient and control groups. The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups) and direct bvFTD-versus-control t-tests and accompanying VBM results are presented. The paper provides MNI stereotactic coordinates for atrophy peaks and reports whole-brain VBM results (tables/figures with MNI coordinates). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, imaging tables/coordinates) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It employed voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as an imaging modality (I3). The sample included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=22) (I4) and an age-matched healthy control group (n=34), exceeding the minimum sample size requirement (I5). The paper reports patient-control (bvFTD vs. controls) group-level comparisons in the VBM analysis (I6), with patient-control group comparisons tested and described. The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other diagnostic groups), satisfying sample purity (I7). The methods describe whole-brain VBM analyses registered to MNI space and report VBM results (including supplementary figures), indicating whole-brain stereotactic reporting consistent with I8. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core article content is present.

This study uses FDG-PET and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (15 bvFTD/fd+), and the patient sample size exceeds 6; however it does NOT report any group-level bvFTD versus healthy control comparison (no recruited control group), nor any whole-brain voxelwise bvFTD>control or bvFTD<control contrasts or stereotactic coordinates. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 (direct patient vs control group comparison) and I8 (whole-brain results in stereotactic space). Because there is no concurrent control group, it also meets exclusion criterion E11 (case series without a control group). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (>=6 patients). Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7 (contrast requirement not applicable because no comparison), I8. Full text appears complete for methods/results/discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study uses VBM (structural MRI) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=28) and healthy controls (n=19), meeting I3, I4, and I5. However, the imaging analyses reported are correlational (voxel-wise regressions of discrepancy scores across a mixed diagnostic sample and polisher/tarnisher subsamples) and do not present a group-level VBM contrast directly comparing the bvFTD group versus healthy controls (e.g., bvFTD < controls). The paper parameterizes diagnosis as covariates and reports regressions across pooled groups rather than a bvFTD vs control whole-brain comparison with stereotactic coordinates. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (direct bvFTD vs control group contrast) is not met; consequently I8 (coordinates for such a contrast) is also not satisfied. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) are triggered.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (bvFTD group size ≥6, n=11). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (imaging modality — study uses tensor-based morphometry [TBM], not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET as required), I6 (no group-level comparison of bvFTD versus healthy controls; comparison is bvFTD versus early-onset AD), I7 (sample-purity criterion for a bvFTD-versus-control comparison cannot be assessed because no healthy-control contrast is reported), and I8 (cannot confirm reported whole-brain stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD>control contrast because that contrast was not performed). No exclusion criteria from the provided list directly apply. Full text appears complete.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry in a large clinically defined bvFTD sample (I3, I4, I5 satisfied). However, it does not report any group-level comparison of bvFTD patients versus a healthy control group; all reported VBM analyses are within the patient group (regressions/correlations with reward-seeking scores). Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (direct bvFTD vs. control group comparison) is not met, and I8 (coordinates for such a comparison) is consequently not applicable/ not met. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (meets I3) and includes sufficient group sizes (meets I5). However, it does not meet the review’s requirement that the sample consists of clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4) because the patient group is a heterogeneous FTD sample (behavioural, language, corticobasal presentations) and the paper does not present a bvFTD-only group. Consequently, it does not provide a bvFTD-versus-healthy-control group-level comparison (I6) nor a bvFTD-specific, pure patient-vs-control contrast (I7). Although whole-brain VBM was performed (and some coordinates are reported), the required bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain coordinate-reporting criterion (I8) is not applicable because no bvFTD group was defined for that comparison. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) appear to be triggered. Full text appears complete and sufficient for this determination.

This paper uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=21) and healthy controls (n=46), fulfilling imaging and sample-size criteria. However, the imaging results are reported as brain–behaviour (discrepancy score) correlations across a heterogeneous pooled sample and secondary ‘‘shared-effects’’ analyses controlling for group membership. The manuscript does not present a direct, group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrast that directly compares the bvFTD group against recruited healthy controls (e.g., bvFTD < controls) as required by I6. Because no pure bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise comparison is reported, the paper fails I6 (CONTRAST) and therefore also does not meet I7 (SAMPLE PURITY) and I8 (COORDINATES for a bvFTD vs control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM), I4 (bvFTD included), I5 (sample sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7, I8. No exclusion criteria from the list were triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=13) against healthy controls (n=12). It explicitly describes group-level bvFTD vs. control contrasts (e.g., “Compared with controls, bvFTD patients showed decreased gray matter intensity...”) and provides results in MNI stereotaxic space (example coordinate x=14, y=-4, z=-16). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD ≥6; controls ≥6). The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8 are met and the paper should be INCLUDED for the review.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the bvFTD meta-analysis: it uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) alongside DTI (I3); includes a clearly defined behavioral-variant FTD group (bvFTD, n=12) diagnosed clinically (I4); has adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=12; controls n=15) exceeding the minimum of 6 (I5); reports group-level cross-sectional voxelwise comparisons of each FTD subtype versus controls (I6); the bvFTD group is analyzed separately rather than pooled with other patient groups (I7); and the analyses are conducted in standard stereotactic space (MNI) with voxelwise, whole-brain VBM/TBSS results reported (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Confident inclusion based on direct bvFTD vs control whole-brain VBM analyses described in the paper.

This full-text empirical study uses resting-state fMRI and VBM (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=15) separate from an ALS group (I4, I7), includes a healthy control group (n=15) and all groups exceed the minimum sample size (I5), and reports group-level, whole-brain comparisons of bvFTD versus controls with Talairach normalization and whole-brain ICA/VBM analyses (I6, I8). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for this review and should be included.

The study is an original empirical VBM investigation published in PLoS One that explicitly includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=23) and healthy controls (n=16), performs whole-brain VBM analyses in MNI space, and reports direct group-level comparisons of bvFTD versus controls with voxelwise results described and displayed. Sample sizes exceed the minimum. The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion (full text present). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the review.

The study uses resting-state fMRI (meets I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD subjects (7 bvFTD cases; meets I4), and has adequate sample sizes (14 patients, 16 controls; meets I5). HOWEVER the paper does not report a group-level comparison of bvFTD alone versus healthy controls. The FTD patient group is pooled (7 bvFTD + 7 avPPA) and all imaging group comparisons are performed on this combined FTD-GRN+ group versus controls. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 (direct bvFTD vs control group-level comparison), I7 (bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups), and I8 (whole-brain coordinates reported for a bvFTD-vs-control comparison) are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria E5–E11 apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because key inclusion criteria I6, I7, and I8 are not met; included criteria met: I3, I4, I5.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the required imaging-modality and whole-brain/coordinated-reporting criteria. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (the imaging analyses are ROI/volume comparisons from FreeSurfer with no whole-brain voxelwise results or stereotactic coordinates reported). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants, pathology/biomarker-confirmed), I5 (sample sizes: bvFTD n=25, controls n=25), I6 (reports group-level bvFTD vs. control comparisons for brain volumes), I7 (bvFTD group is reported separately, not pooled with other patient groups). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is structural volumetry and PiB amyloid PET as biomarker — not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I8 (no whole-brain stereotactic-coordinate results reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because I3 and I8 are not satisfied and E6 applies, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This study applies voxel-based morphometry (VBM) within a unified VBM+TBM framework and reports whole-brain SPM comparisons between a frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patient group (N=30) and healthy controls (N=14). It therefore meets the modality criterion (I3), includes an FTD patient group (I4) with sufficient sample size (I5), performs direct group-level FTD vs control comparisons (I6), keeps the FTD group separate from other patient groups (I7), and reports whole-brain SPM results (I8). The only ambiguity is that the paper labels the clinical group as “FTD” rather than explicitly stating the behavioral variant (bvFTD). Given the paper’s reported whole-brain VBM analyses of an FTD group with typical bvFTD-like atrophy patterns and the review instruction to include when in doubt, I include this study as relevant to bvFTD-related morphometry.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry and task-free (resting-state) fMRI (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with group sizes of 14 patients and 14+ controls (I5); reports group-level voxelwise comparisons of bvFTD groups versus healthy controls for both VBM and functional connectivity (I6); bvFTD groups are analyzed as bvFTD (not pooled with other dementia syndromes) despite some comorbid bvFTD-MND cases (I7); and the study describes whole-brain voxelwise analyses referenced to a stereotactic template and displays voxelwise results (I8). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are noted but not required. No exclusion criteria are triggered by the provided full text.

This paper uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (and reports whole-brain analyses) and diffusion imaging (I3). It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=11) and healthy controls (n=14) (I4, I5). Group-level VBM and DTI contrasts comparing each patient group, including bvFTD, directly against Controls are reported (bvFTD vs Controls) (I6). The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups) (I7). Results are reported in stereotactic space with MNI coordinates given for VBM findings (e.g., x=−14,y=10,z=−22) (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

While this study clearly investigates bvFTD and uses VBM (I3), includes a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD sample (N=20) and healthy controls (N=31) meeting the minimum sample-size requirement (I4, I5), it does NOT report any group-level whole-brain imaging contrast that directly compares the bvFTD group against healthy controls (i.e., no bvFTD vs control VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET comparison). Imaging analyses were restricted to within-group correlations in the bvFTD participants only. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (direct bvFTD vs control group comparison) is not met, and consequently I7 and I8 (requirements tied to that between-group contrast) are also not met. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) apply. Recommendation: EXCLUDE due to failure to meet I6 (and thus I7, I8).

This study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes a bvFTD subgroup (47 bvFTD patients) with adequate sample sizes and healthy controls. However, the imaging analyses reported are within-patient VBM correlations relating atrophy to happiness behavior (patient-only correlational analyses). The paper does not report any group-level whole-brain voxelwise comparison that directly contrasts a bvFTD patient group against a healthy control group (e.g., bvFTD < controls). Behavioral group comparisons (FTD vs controls) were reported for facial and physiological measures, but no bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain VBM (or fMRI/FDG-PET) contrast with stereotactic coordinates is presented. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (direct bvFTD vs healthy control group-level imaging contrast) is not met, so the study must be excluded.

This article uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports whole-brain VBM analyses. It includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) group (n=18) and a healthy control group (n=18), meeting the minimum sample-size requirement. The paper reports direct group-level contrasts comparing controls > bvFTD (VBM contrasts) and presents whole-brain results (figures, tables, and supplemental material referenced, with MNI coordinates mentioned). The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups) for the bvFTD-versus-control comparison. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because the bvFTD patient group contains only 5 participants, which fails inclusion criterion I5 (minimum 6 patients). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM and [18F]FDG-PET), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I6 (reports group-level bvFTD vs control voxel-wise comparisons), I7 (bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups), and I8 (whole-brain voxel-wise results with reported local maxima/coordinates). No exclusion criteria are triggered by the content provided. The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, tables/references present). Given the definitive sample-size shortfall, the study must be excluded despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

This paper reports a voxel-based morphometry-style whole-brain T1 MRI analysis (GM density) comparing bvFTD patients to healthy seniors, with images warped into MNI space and permutation-based voxelwise group comparisons and regressions. The sample comprises 12 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 14 healthy controls (both >6). The manuscript describes and reports group-level bvFTD versus control comparisons (bvFTD < controls) and relates behavioral performance to GM atrophy; analyses are whole-brain in stereotactic space (MNI) and results/figures/tables are reported. The bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups. Full article text includes intro, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are referenced. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) are met and the study should be included.

This study is relevant to bvFTD and uses FDG-PET and VBM, includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=8 symptomatic) and healthy non-carrier controls (n=8), and reports group-level comparisons (including SC vs NC) for ROI measures. However, the paper did not report whole-brain voxel-wise results (with stereotactic coordinates) specifically for the bvFTD (symptomatic carriers) versus healthy control comparison — the voxel-wise whole-brain analyses were performed for mutation carriers (symptomatic + asymptomatic) versus non-carriers, and the authors state they lacked power to perform voxel-wise comparisons among the three diagnostic groups. Because inclusion criterion I8 (whole-brain coordinates for the bvFTD-versus-control comparison) is not met, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) apply.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD subjects as a sporadic FTD group) and I5 (bvFTD patient group size ≥6; n=15). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (imaging modality – study uses longitudinal structural MRI with tensor-based morphometry/atrophy measures, not Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM), task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no group-level bvFTD versus healthy control comparison reported), and I8 (no reported whole-brain stereotactic-coordinate results for a bvFTD-vs-control contrast). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Because required imaging modality and the critical bvFTD-vs-control contrast are absent, the paper must be excluded.

This task-based fMRI study directly compares clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15) to healthy controls (n=11) using group-level two-sample t-tests and reports significant between-group contrasts (text references to tables/SPMs with thresholding and small-volume/whole-brain FWE). Imaging modality (task fMRI), sample diagnosis, sample sizes, direct bvFTD-versus-control group analyses, sample purity (bvFTD group not pooled with other syndromes), and reporting of whole-brain results are all satisfied or clearly described. The supplied full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review, ROI-only, non-FDG PET, connectivity-only, case report) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This empirical study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports group-level VBM comparisons of bvFTD patients (n=13) versus healthy controls (n=11). The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups), sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6), and the VBM methods state results were aligned to MNI space with voxel coordinates provided. The full text includes methods, results and VBM group contrasts versus controls. No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes a separately reported bvFTD group (n=14) (I4) and healthy controls (n=28) with adequate sample sizes (I5); reports group-level VBM comparisons of bvFTD versus controls (I6); the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups for that comparison (I7); analyses and figures are presented in MNI space with stereotactic coordinates indicated/overlayed (I8). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria from the review are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the bvFTD meta-analysis.

This study uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with a large sample, but it does not report a group-level direct comparison of a bvFTD patient group versus a healthy control group (bvFTD < controls or controls > bvFTD). The imaging analyses focus on voxelwise correlates of "disgusting behaviors" across a heterogeneous patient sample and within-group ROI analyses (bvFTD and svPPA) rather than an independent bvFTD-versus-healthy control whole-brain contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (direct bvFTD vs healthy control group-level comparison). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM), I4 (bvFTD sample present), I5 (sample sizes >6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no bvFTD vs control group-level comparison). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion requirements for the review: it includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) group (n=12) compared with a control group (n=10); uses FDG-PET as an imaging modality (alongside ASL); reports group-level voxel-wise SPM comparisons of bvFTD versus controls; and indicates whole-brain results in stereotactic space (MNI coordinates reported and referenced in supplementary tables). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). The full text contains Introduction, Methods (including imaging and voxel-wise analysis), Results (group comparisons, correlations, ROC/AUC) and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (FDG tracer used, whole-brain analyses performed, not a review or ROI-only study, not a case report). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (24 bvFTD in behavioural cohort; imaging sample includes 18 bvFTD) (I4); sample sizes meet the minimum (bvFTD n=18 for imaging, controls n=15) (I5); it reports group-level whole-brain VBM comparisons directly contrasting patient groups with healthy controls (bvFTD vs controls) (I6); the bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups) (I7); analyses were performed in standard stereotactic space (MNI) and MNI coordinates are reported for imaging results (I8). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are met. Given these points, the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of bvFTD VBM studies.

This study used VBM (I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=22) (I4) and meets the sample size criterion for the patient group (I5). However, the imaging analyses reported are within-patient VBM correlations of hedonic symptoms across FTLD and separate analyses within AD; there is no reported group-level VBM contrast directly comparing a bvFTD group against a recruited healthy control group (criterion I6 not met). Because no bvFTD-versus-control contrast is reported, sample-purity for such a contrast (I7) and the requirement to report stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD vs control comparison (I8) are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore the paper must be excluded from this review.

This study is excluded because it does not report a group-level VBM comparison of the bvFTD patient group directly versus a healthy control group (required inclusion criterion I6). (a) Exclusion criteria met: None ([]) . (b) Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD participants), I5 (patient and control group sizes meet the ≥6 threshold). (c) Inclusion criteria NOT satisfied: I6 (no reported bvFTD-versus-control group-level contrast; VBM analyses were correlations within patients and within bvFTD subgroup rather than a direct bvFTD vs control comparison), I7 (bvFTD-versus-control contrast not present so purity requirement for that contrast cannot be assessed/satisfied), I8 (no evidence in the paper of reported stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrast). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Because failing any one required inclusion criterion mandates exclusion, I exclude this paper.

This paper reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12 on placebo; 10–12 included in imaging analyses) against healthy controls (n=20), with between-group t-tests and SPM/DARTEL normalization to MNI space and cluster-based FWE thresholding. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6 per group). The manuscript explicitly describes whole-brain VBM contrasts of bvFTD versus controls, including thresholding and figures of atrophy, indicating reporting in stereotactic space. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (VBM), Results (group VBM findings), and Discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study does not use any of the eligible imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). It is an MRI structural study using manual ROI tracing and shape analysis of the caudate and putamen (region-of-interest approach) rather than whole-brain voxelwise VBM/fMRI/FDG analyses; therefore it meets exclusion E6 (ROI-only, no whole-brain results). The paper does meet several inclusion criteria (I4: clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample; I5: adequate sample size, 28 patients and 26 controls; I6: direct bvFTD versus healthy control group comparison; I7: bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups). However I3 (required imaging modality) is not satisfied, and I8 (reporting whole-brain stereotactic coordinates) is not fulfilled. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry analyses and explicitly includes a separately analyzed behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) group (n=59) and healthy controls (n=61). The manuscript describes voxel-wise group-level contrasts of bvFTD versus controls, and indicates coordinates/local maxima are provided in Supplementary Tables, satisfying reporting in stereotactic space. Sample sizes exceed the minimum. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not using disallowed modalities/tracers, not a case series). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so appears complete.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (N=20) (I4) and a healthy control group (N=20), both ≥6 participants (I5); reports a direct group-level VBM comparison between bvFTD and controls (two-sample t-test) (I6); the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups (I7); and the paper reports voxel-wise/regression results in stereotactic space (MNI coordinates are given for the IFG peak: −41, 26, 3) (I8). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply. Hence the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical neuroimaging study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=29) and healthy controls (n=37), uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) alongside DTI, and reports group-level comparisons and whole-brain analyses. The paper describes generating disease maps for each syndromic group (bvFTD and svPPA) relative to a matched healthy cohort, and reports voxelwise VBM and TBSS results with cluster/peak reporting procedures (SPM8, randomise, cluster extraction), consistent with whole-brain stereotactic reporting. The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled) and sample sizes exceed the minimum. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study should be excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain reporting requirements. Exclusion (a): E6 applies — the imaging analysis is manual hypothalamic volumetry (ROI tracing) on structural MRI with no whole-brain voxelwise results or stereotactic coordinates reported. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD group), I5 (sample sizes meet minimum: bvFTD n=19, controls n=23), I6 (reports group-level bvFTD versus control comparisons), and I7 (bvFTD group is analyzed separately, not pooled). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) and I8 (no whole-brain, stereotactic-coordinate results reported). Full text appears complete for screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Given the review’s requirement for whole-brain VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET voxelwise coordinates, this paper is not eligible.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: E6 — the paper does not report whole-brain, stereotactic-coordinate results for an FTD-vs-control voxelwise contrast; analyses are multivariate SVM classification and summary performance (AUC/PPV/NPV) rather than whole-brain coordinate tables. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 — VBM-style preprocessing/voxelwise gray-matter maps were used; I5 — patient and control group sizes meet the >=6 requirement (FTD n=12; HC n=18). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I4 — the FTD group is not specified as behavioral variant (bvFTD)/Pick’s disease; authors state “FTD (without distinguishing subtypes)”; I6 — no reported group-level voxelwise contrast that directly compares a bvFTD patient group versus healthy controls; I8 — no whole-brain stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) are provided for an FTD-vs-control comparison in the text. Full text appears complete for methods/results/discussion, so not marked incomplete.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports whole-brain VBM analyses.
