Sample purity: bvFTD is reported as a separate group (not pooled with other patient groups) and compared to controls. Coordinates/results reporting: VBM results and maximum coordinates are reported in MNI space. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only analysis, non-qualifying modality) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This FDG-PET study includes 52 clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (meets I3, I4, I5, I7 and reports whole-brain SPM analyses suggesting I8). However, the required group-level bvFTD-versus-healthy-control contrast (I6) is not satisfied: the authors compare patients to a normative FDG-PET image database (n=112) rather than to a recruited healthy control group, and the protocol explicitly uses database comparisons for single-subject and group analyses. Per the review’s criteria, comparisons against a normative image database do NOT meet I6, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) are triggered.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used voxel-based morphometry and resting-state/task fMRI (I3); included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (I4); had adequate sample sizes (14 bvFTD, 19 controls) exceeding the ≥6 threshold (I5); reported direct group-level comparisons between bvFTD and healthy controls (VBM and resting-state connectivity two-sample tests) (I6); the bvFTD group was not pooled with other patient groups (I7); and the paper reports stereotactic coordinates for key contrasts (e.g., ATL [-45,13,-37], IFG [-52,2,14]) and describes whole-brain VBM results (I8). No exclusion criteria were triggered based on the provided full text. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This study uses whole-brain voxelwise longitudinal MRI methods consistent with VBM-style analyses (I3 satisfied). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4 satisfied) and has adequate sample sizes in patient and control groups (I5 satisfied). However, the primary voxelwise comparisons reported combine bvFTD and svPPA into a single FTLD group and compare that combined group to controls. The paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain contrast of bvFTD patients alone versus healthy controls, so it fails to meet the required direct bvFTD-vs-control contrast (I6 not met) and violates the sample-purity requirement that bvFTD must not be pooled with other patient groups in the bvFTD-vs-control comparison (I7 not met). Because the required bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise comparison is absent, I8 (coordinates for that comparison) is also not met. Therefore the paper must be excluded.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); included clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (n=34) and healthy controls (n=30) (I4,I5); reports group-level VBM contrasts directly comparing bvFTD groups to healthy controls (I6); the bvFTD groups are not pooled with other patient groups (I7); and the paper describes whole-brain VBM results with supplementary figures/tables (I8). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria from the review apply. Therefore I include this study for the meta-analysis.

This study uses VBM (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bv-FTD subgroup (n=15) (I4), and has adequate group sizes including controls (n=15) (I5). However it does NOT report any group-level whole-brain comparison that directly contrasts bvFTD patients versus healthy controls (I6 not met). The VBM analyses presented compare a mixed “poor melody” patient subgroup (mixed diagnoses) to controls and perform correlations with all patients merged; bvFTD is not isolated for a bvFTD-vs-control contrast (I7 not met). While the paper reports whole-brain VBM results for other contrasts, there is no bvFTD-specific voxelwise comparison with controls and thus it fails the required contrast and sample-purity criteria. No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical longitudinal study using resting-state fMRI and VBM (I3 satisfied). It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) alongside AD and healthy control groups (n=22) meeting the sample requirements (I4, I5). The paper reports direct group-level voxel-wise comparisons between bvFTD and healthy controls (bvFTD < controls reported at follow-up) using whole-brain analyses with nonparametric permutation testing and FWE correction, and refers to coordinate tables/figures (I6, I8). The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups), satisfying sample purity (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, ROI-only, non-empirical design, inappropriate imaging modality, or case-series issues). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion; therefore inclusion is appropriate.

This empirical study includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=26) and healthy controls (n=22), uses voxel-based morphometry and resting-state fMRI, and reports group-level bvFTD versus control comparisons (whole-brain VBM results with peak coordinates referenced in Supplementary Tables). The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled), meeting sample size and contrast requirements. Core article content (methods, results, discussion) is present; supplementary coordinate tables are cited. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses FDG‐PET as an imaging modality alongside ASL‐MRI (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=32) (I4) and a healthy control group (n=15), both >6 participants (I5); reports group-level voxel-wise and multivariate (PLS logistic regression and GLM) comparisons of bvFTD versus controls (I6) with whole-brain normalized images and statistical parametric maps (images were normalized to a template and voxel-wise GLMs thresholded with FDR), which satisfies the requirement for whole-brain results in stereotactic space per review guidance (I8). The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled) meeting sample purity (I7). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not a review, not ROI-only, uses FDG tracer, not case series). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical VBM study of behavioural-variant FTD that meets all inclusion criteria. Imaging modality: whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) was used. Sample: includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=36) and an FTD-ALS group (n=20) with healthy controls (n=23); all groups exceed the N>=6 requirement. Contrast: group-level comparisons between patient groups and healthy controls are reported, and bvFTD is analyzed as a separate group (bvFTD vs. controls), not pooled with other syndromes. Sample purity: bvFTD is reported separately from FTD-ALS and compared with controls. Coordinates: whole-brain stereotactic results (MNI) are described and reported (supplementary tables e2/e3). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not a review, not ROI-only, not an excluded modality, not a case report). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore the study should be included for the review.

This is an empirical resting-state fMRI study that includes a separate clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=21) and healthy controls (n=25). The paper reports group-level whole-brain ICA and dual-regression comparisons directly contrasting bvFTD versus controls, with results reported in MNI space (methods describe MNI152 registration and results reference MNI coordinates). Sample is not pooled with other patient groups. Imaging modality, sample size, between-group contrast, sample purity, and stereotactic whole-brain reporting meet the review inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This study used Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) and included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=58) with healthy controls, meeting imaging and sample-size criteria. However, the imaging analyses reported are voxelwise brain–behavior correlations across a mixed diagnostic sample and coatrophy checks; the paper does not report a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise comparison directly contrasting bvFTD patients versus healthy controls (e.g., bvFTD < controls). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (direct bvFTD vs control group comparison). No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) are met. Full text appears to contain core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review. It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=16) and a healthy control group (n=22) meeting the minimum sample-size threshold, and performed group-level bvFTD versus control whole-brain comparisons (reported as VBM results normalized to MNI space with FWE-corrected statistics). The bvFTD group was analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups). Whole-brain stereotactic analyses are described in the methods and results (MNI normalization via DARTEL), so criterion for reporting results in stereotactic space is satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study uses FDG-PET voxel-based analyses (SPM8) normalized to MNI space and reports group-level voxelwise comparisons of a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group versus healthy controls. Sample sizes meet thresholds (26 bvFTD, 24 controls). The paper describes whole-brain SPM results (clusters, Brodmann areas) and references supplementary tables for detailed maps/coordinates. bvFTD group was not pooled with other patient groups. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not include a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group nor report a direct bvFTD-versus-control group comparison. Instead, the sample consists of presymptomatic C9ORF72 expansion carriers compared to healthy controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM and resting-state fMRI) and I5 (patient group n=15 and control groups ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participants are not clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease patients), I6 (no group-level bvFTD vs. healthy control contrast reported), I7 (no bvFTD group to assess sample purity), and I8 (no whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control stereotactic coordinates to report). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper is not eligible for inclusion in this bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it is an empirical VBM study (I3) of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with 52 patients and 52 controls (I5). It reports group-level VBM comparisons directly contrasting bvFTD versus healthy controls (I6), the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups (I7), and whole-brain analyses were performed with images normalized to MNI space and reported (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. The supplied full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and Conclusion, so fulltext appears complete.

Although this paper uses whole-brain VBM (I3), includes a separate bvFTD patient group (n=16) (I4), and has adequate group sizes including controls (I5), it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise comparison that directly contrasts the bvFTD group against healthy controls (I6 not met). The VBM analyses described are brain–behavior correlations across the entire sample and co-atrophy checks controlling for group membership, rather than a bvFTD vs. control voxelwise contrast with stereotactic coordinates (I8 not met). Therefore it fails to meet the required imaging-group comparison inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) appear to be triggered by the provided full text. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This study uses FDG-PET (also ASL) and includes clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD cases with sufficient sample sizes (FTD n=20; controls n=38), so it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4 and I5. However, it does not report a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise comparison of a bvFTD-only patient group versus healthy controls (analyses are based on subject-level Z-maps and visual reader assessments rather than a group contrast), and no stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD-vs-control contrast are provided. Additionally, the FTD patient group is mixed across subtypes (behavioural variant and semantic dementia at one site), violating the sample-purity requirement. Therefore inclusion criteria I6, I7 and I8 are not met. No listed exclusion criteria (E5–E11) directly apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical longitudinal voxel-wise analysis of T1-weighted MRI (voxel-based morphometry–style longitudinal change maps) comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=44) to a healthy control group (n=97). The study performs group-level voxelwise t-statistic comparisons between bvFTD and controls, treats bvFTD as a separate group (not pooled with other FTLD variants), and reports whole-brain analyses after warping to MNI space. Sample sizes exceed the ≥6 threshold for patients and controls. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This VBM study does not include a clinically defined behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease patient group and therefore does not address the review objective. It reports voxelwise comparisons of pathologically-defined groups (AD, DLB, 3R-tau, 4R-tau, TDP43A, TDP43C) versus controls and between pathology groups, but no bvFTD clinical group is described or directly compared with healthy controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I5 (patient groups and control group sizes >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (sample does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease), I6 (no group-level bvFTD vs healthy control comparison), I7 (no bvFTD group to assess sample purity), I8 (no report of bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain coordinates because that comparison was not performed). No exclusion criteria from E5–E11 apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an original, multicenter empirical study using resting-state fMRI and VBM (imaging modalities within scope). It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=52) and matched healthy controls (n=60), and reports group-level bvFTD versus control comparisons (VBM and whole-brain functional connectivity/graph-theory analyses). The methods state normalization to MNI space and report whole-brain VBM results (with Supporting Information tables), satisfying coordinate reporting expectations per screening guidance. The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled). Full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the review.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (imaging subset bvFTD n=14) with a control group (n=27). However, the neuroimaging analyses report correlations between PCA-derived behavioural components and grey/white matter across the transdiagnostic cohort, not a group-level voxelwise comparison that directly contrasts a bvFTD-only patient group against healthy controls. Therefore it does not satisfy the required contrast criterion for inclusion. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD participants included), I5 (patient and control sample sizes meet minima). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no direct bvFTD vs control group-level comparison), I7 (bvFTD not analyzed as an isolated group in the required contrast), I8 (no bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria from the review list apply to this paper. Full text appears complete for screening.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses VBM (FSL-VBM) as an imaging modality (I3); it includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=7) (I4) and a healthy control group (n=40) with adequate sample sizes (I5); it reports group-level, whole-brain comparisons of single phenotypes versus controls including bvFTD vs controls (I6) and the bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled) (I7). Whole-brain voxelwise results were produced in MNI152 space and figures indicate MNI coordinates (I8). No exclusion criteria appear to be violated (no review, no ROI-only, modalities acceptable, not a case report). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion; supplementary files not required to judge. Therefore INCLUDE.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI (allowed modality) along with cortical thickness and DTI (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=27) (I4); has sufficient sample sizes (bvFTD n=27, controls n=48) (I5); reports group-level direct comparisons of bvFTD versus healthy controls with whole-brain analyses (cortical thickness, TBSS, dual-regression RS-fMRI) (I6); the bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled) (I7); and the methods describe whole-brain results in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-only FC, PET tracer is not relevant). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=25) (I4) and a healthy control group (n=25) meeting sample size requirements (I5); reports direct voxel-wise group-level comparisons of bvFTD versus controls (I6) with whole-brain analyses in MNI space and states that maximum voxel coordinates are provided (I8); the bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups) (I7). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and neuroimaging analyses.

This study is excluded because it uses whole-brain cortical thickness analyses derived from structural MRI (vertex-by-vertex cortical thickness), not one of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). This violates exclusion criterion E9 (studies that only report cortical thickness methods are ineligible). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (sample sizes: 88 patients, 30 controls), I6 (group-level bvFTD versus healthy control comparisons reported), I7 (bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups), and I8 (whole-brain comparisons described). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (required imaging modality). Full text appears complete for screening.

The study reports whole-brain voxel-wise gray matter (GM) analyses comparing bvFTD (n=32) to healthy controls (n=17) using Randomise in FSL, and summarizes peak atrophy/regressions (table e-1 and figures). The bvFTD sample is clinically diagnosed and not pooled with other patient groups; sample sizes meet thresholds. The paper describes and reports a direct group-level bvFTD vs control comparison and whole-brain results in stereotactic space (peaks provided in supplemental table). Thus it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (VBM-style whole-brain MRI comparison of bvFTD vs controls). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to assess grey matter (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=19) (I4); sample sizes meet minimums with bvFTD n=19 and healthy controls n=20 (I5); reports group-level voxel-wise comparisons directly contrasting patient groups with healthy controls (two-sample t-tests) (I6); bvFTD patients are analyzed as a separate group (not pooled with other patient groups) (I7); and the paper describes whole-brain VBM analyses in stereotactic space using SPM/DARTEL consistent with reporting coordinates or maps (I8). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It reports FDG-PET imaging (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=90 overall; n=12 underwent PET) (I4,I5). The paper describes voxelwise group comparisons of glucose metabolism against a healthy control group and gives subtype-specific hypometabolism results (bvFTD described separately) satisfying the requirement for a direct bvFTD-versus-control group-level contrast (I6) and that the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups for that comparison (I7). Whole-brain voxelwise analysis using SPM8 is described (voxel-by-voxel 2-sample t-test, thresholds reported), indicating whole-brain stereotactic analyses were performed (I8). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical resting-state fMRI study that directly compares a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=38) to age-matched healthy controls (n=32) using whole-brain graph/connectional analyses (network-based statistics). It satisfies imaging modality (I3: rs-fMRI), sample includes bvFTD patients (I4), sample sizes exceed the 6-participant minimum for patient and control groups (I5), and it reports group-level bvFTD versus control comparisons (I6). The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled with other diagnoses) (I7). The paper describes whole-brain network results and node lists/tables (table e-1) consistent with stereotactic reporting of results (I8). Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary tables are referenced. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Although this study uses voxel-based morphometry and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group and healthy controls with adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=24 with MRI, controls n=21), it does not report any whole-brain, group-level VBM comparison directly contrasting bvFTD versus healthy controls. The VBM analyses described are multiple regressions performed within the bvFTD patient group correlating atrophy with behavioural valence scores, not a bvFTD < controls (or controls > bvFTD) voxelwise comparison. Therefore Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (>=6 participants per group). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no group-level bvFTD vs control imaging comparison), I8 (no report of whole-brain bvFTD-vs-control stereotactic coordinates). No exclusion criteria from the provided list (E5–E11) apply. Full text appears complete for methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Because failure to meet required inclusion criterion I6 prevents eligibility for this meta-analysis, the study is excluded.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM)-style whole-brain grey matter W-score maps and frequency maps derived from comparisons to healthy controls, meeting the imaging modality and analysis requirements. The sample consists of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=117, with subgroup analyses) exceeding the minimum group size. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise analyses comparing bvFTD patients to controls (W-score maps, frequency maps, and voxel-wise PCA/linear discriminant analyses). Although coordinate tables are not visible in the provided excerpt, the manuscript describes whole-brain voxel-wise comparisons and figures of thresholded maps, and per instructions such descriptions suffice to treat coordinate reporting as met. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present; supplementary materials are noted but not required for inclusion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (N=20; VBM sample N=17) and healthy controls (N=39; VBM controls N=28). The paper reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry group comparisons (bvFTD vs. controls) and describes anatomically localized atrophy using an MNI template; voxelwise correlations and whole-brain results with stereotactic coordinates are reported for some analyses. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6 per group). The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups). The paper contains full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only, non-eligible imaging modality, case report) apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

Excluded because the imaging analysis does not meet the review’s required modalities and reporting. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study reports ROI-based volumetric analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants), I5 (bvFTD subgroup size >=6, n=26). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (study does not use VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no group-level bvFTD versus healthy control voxelwise contrast reported), I7 (no bvFTD-versus-control comparison to assess purity), I8 (no whole-brain stereotactic coordinates reported for a bvFTD vs control contrast). Full text appears complete. Because the review requires VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET voxelwise group comparisons against healthy controls with coordinates, this paper (FreeSurfer ROI volumetry across mixed patient groups without bvFTD-vs-control voxelwise contrasts) does not satisfy key inclusion criteria.

This study directly addresses bvFTD using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with whole-brain SPM/DARTEL analyses. It includes 20 clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients and 20 healthy controls (both >6), and reports direct group-level bvFTD versus control comparisons (bvFTD < HC) with stereotactic coordinates (e.g., cluster maxima reported in MNI space). The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (subgroups reported but not pooled with other patient syndromes), satisfying sample purity. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (full article content present). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not DTI-only, PET tracer is not relevant). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

The study uses FDG-PET and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with adequate sample sizes, but it does not provide a group-level comparison of bvFTD-only patients versus healthy controls. Instead, analyses compare a combined FTD patient group (mixed subtypes including bvFTD, svPPA, nfPPA, and possible bvFTD) against controls. This violates the requirement that the bvFTD group not be pooled with other patient groups and that there be a bvFTD-versus-control group-level contrast. No exclusion criteria from the list are directly met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (bvFTD participants included in sample), I5 (≥6 patients and ≥6 controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no bvFTD-specific group-level comparison vs controls), I7 (sample purity: bvFTD not isolated from other FTD subtypes). I8 (coordinates/reporting of whole-brain stereotactic results) appears not clearly satisfied for a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain contrast. Therefore exclude.

This study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on genetic FTD mutation carriers versus noncarrier controls and has adequate group sizes, but it does not report analyses that directly compare a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group against healthy controls. Specifically: (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 (uses VBM), I5 (patient and control groups >=6 participants), I8 (whole-brain voxel-wise results reported using SPM and voxel-level FWE correction). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I4 (sample is not explicitly clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease patients — participants are genetic mutation carriers with heterogeneous clinical manifestations), I6 (no group-level direct bvFTD-versus-healthy-control comparison), I7 (the patient group is mutation-carrier-based and pooled across genetic/clinical presentations rather than a bvFTD-only group). Therefore it does not satisfy the review’s requirement for bvFTD-versus-control comparisons and must be excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (patient group size ≥6; FTD n=23). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality) — study uses structural linear MRI (Bifrontal Index), not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET; I4 (sample) — reports FTD broadly but does not specify clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease; I6 (contrast) — no group-level comparison of bvFTD versus healthy controls (study compares AD vs FTD, with no healthy control group). No exclusion criteria from the provided list explicitly apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded.

All required inclusion criteria are met. The study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for structural MRI and resting-state fMRI (fALFF) as imaging modalities (I3). The sample comprises 13 clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (I4) and 19 healthy controls, satisfying the minimum group sizes (I5). The paper reports group-level whole-brain comparisons between bvFTD and controls (e.g., two-sample t-test Ctrl > bvFTD for GM volume) meeting the direct bvFTD-versus-control contrast requirement (I6). The bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups (I7). Images were normalized to MNI space and results are described in stereotactic coordinates/space (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E11) apply to this empirical, whole-brain VBM and resting-state fMRI study. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study uses FDG-PET and includes 37 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, satisfying imaging and sample-size criteria. However, it does not report a group-level comparison of a recruited bvFTD patient group directly against a healthy control group. Instead, patient scans were compared to a normative image database and the main analyses are within-patient regressions relating occupation measures to hypometabolism. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (direct bvFTD vs healthy control group comparison) is not met, and consequently I7 and I8 (which pertain to that comparison and reporting coordinates) are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria from E5–E11 apply. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) group (I4) with adequate sample size (19 bvFTD; 16 with MRI available) and a healthy control group (20) (I5); reports direct group-level bvFTD versus control comparisons of grey-matter integrity (e.g. bvFTD < controls) using whole-brain analyses (I6); the bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups) (I7); and VBM was performed in standard stereotactic space (MNI) with whole-brain results reported (figures/tables and Supplementary material referenced) (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only restriction, no disqualifying imaging modality, not a review, not a case report). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This paper reports voxel-based morphometry (voxelwise grey matter density) analyses comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (N=63) to demographically-matched healthy controls (N=55). The methods describe whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL randomise, permutation testing) and report clusters surviving correction; peak loci are reported (MNI to Talairach conversion noted, Table 3). The bvFTD group is analyzed as a distinct group (other FTD phenotypes excluded). Sample sizes exceed the minimum. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (VBM modality, bvFTD sample, adequate sample sizes, direct bvFTD vs control group comparison, group not pooled with other diagnoses, and whole-brain stereotactic coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the imaging modality is tau PET using 18F-flortaucipir rather than FDG-PET, which violates exclusion criterion E10. The study does meet several inclusion criteria: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (sample size >=6: 20 bvFTD patients and 20 controls), I6 (reports direct group-level bvFTD vs healthy control comparisons), I7 (bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups), and I8 (voxel-based whole-brain comparisons reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (required imaging modality VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). Full text appears complete and sufficient for screening.

This is an empirical study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=30) that uses FDG-PET and reports voxel-based whole-brain analyses (VBM) and voxel-based DTI group comparisons versus a healthy control group (N=42). The bvFTD sample is not pooled with other patient groups, and group-level comparisons (ANCOVA/voxel-wise analyses using SPM8 in stereotactic space after normalization) are reported. Although PET was assessed versus a normative database for individual reads, the paper also reports whole-brain voxel-wise group comparisons (VBM/DTI) against recruited controls. Therefore it meets the review’s imaging-modality, sample-size, group-contrast, sample-purity, and whole-brain coordinate-reporting criteria (methods indicate stereotactic normalization). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients that includes a direct group-level voxel-wise comparison against healthy controls. Imaging modality and analysis: voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on T1 MRI with non-linear registration to MNI space, TFCE and FWE correction, and reported cluster/coordinate results (Supplementary Table 3). Sample: bvFTD group (N=35 overall; VBM subgroup N=12) and controls (N=29 overall; VBM subgroup N=20) — both exceed the minimum of 6. Contrast: a two-sample t-test contrasting bvFTD patients and controls was performed and whole-brain results are reported/labelled in stereotactic space. No exclusion criteria from the review apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion); supplementary coordinates are referenced. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is an empirical study that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=23) and healthy controls (n=35), uses voxel-wise anatomical MRI (voxel-based GM density), DTI (TBSS), and resting-state fMRI (ICA-based functional connectivity). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (I5). The paper performs group-level between-group analyses and classification analyses that directly contrast bvFTD versus controls, and describes whole-brain voxel-wise processing (VBM-like GM densities, TBSS skeleton, and ICA components), consistent with whole-brain stereotactic analyses (I6,I8). The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups) fulfilling sample purity (I7). Imaging modalities include VBM/structural and rs-fMRI satisfying modality criterion (I3). No exclusion criteria apply based on the provided full text (not a review, not ROI-only, not PET non-FDG, not case report). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion); supplemental coordinate tables may exist. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion.

This is an empirical VBM study that directly compares a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD group against healthy controls. Imaging modality: whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) was used. Sample: 69 bvFTD patients (>=6) and 28 healthy controls (>=6). Contrast: the paper reports group-level t tests comparing bvFTD vs controls (bvFTD vs control; AD vs control; bvFTD vs AD). Sample purity: the bvFTD group is analysed separately (not pooled with other patient groups). Coordinates/stereotactic reporting: the manuscript states results were overlaid on an MNI standard brain and that maximum voxel coordinates are provided in stereotaxic space; whole-brain results are described. No exclusion criteria from the review are met. Full text appears complete (includes background, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses FDG-PET and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=19) plus healthy controls (n=19), and reports within-group and correlational voxelwise/ROI analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET imaging), I4 (bvFTD group present), I5 (sample sizes ≥6 for patient and control groups), I7 (bvFTD group analyzed separately, not pooled). However, the paper does not report any group-level voxelwise or whole-brain stereotactic-space contrast directly comparing bvFTD versus healthy controls (e.g., bvFTD < controls) with coordinate tables or reported between-group statistical maps. Therefore I6 (direct bvFTD vs control group comparison) is not satisfied, and I8 (reported coordinates for such a bvFTD-vs-control whole-brain comparison) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) are triggered by the available full text. Because at least one required inclusion criterion (I6 and I8) is not met, the study must be excluded.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI (I3), includes a clearly defined clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (50 bvFTD patients) (I4), and includes an adequate sample size with 50 bvFTD patients and 32 healthy controls (I5). The paper reports direct group-level comparisons between bvFTD and healthy controls (bvFTD vs controls) (I6). The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups) (I7). Whole-brain analyses were performed with registration to MNI space and network-based/graph-theory whole-brain results are reported, satisfying the coordinate/whole-brain reporting requirement as described in the methods and results (I8). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria from the list are met.

This is a genetic case-family report with imaging on an index bvFTD patient and a few relatives; it does not meet the review’s sample size or group-comparison requirements. Exclusion IDs met: E11 (case report/case series without a control group). Inclusion IDs met: I3 (uses FDG‑PET imaging) and I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient(s)). Inclusion IDs NOT met: I5 (minimum N≥6 patients in the patient group), I6 (no group-level bvFTD versus healthy control comparison reported), I7 (no bvFTD-versus-control comparison; patient data are not a bvFTD group compared to controls), I8 (no whole-brain group-level stereotactic coordinates reported). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an original empirical VBM study that directly addresses bvFTD. The study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on 3T T1-weighted MRI (meets I3). It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=45) and a healthy control group (n=35) (meets I4 and I5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain VBM contrasts comparing each patient group (including bvFTD alone) against controls (bvFTD vs controls) (meets I6 and I7). Whole-brain analyses are described and results are reported with figures/tables (meets I8; coordinate reporting is described in text and tables/figures are referenced). No exclusion criteria are met: this is not a review/meta-analysis (E5), not an ROI-only or non-eligible modality study (E6, E9, E10), not a case report/series (E11), and the sample excludes comorbid psychiatric/other dementias as required. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review of bvFTD imaging studies.

This study is excluded because it does not use an eligible imaging modality (it is a tau PET study using 18F-THK5351 rather than FDG-PET) and reports region-of-interest (VOI) SUVR results without whole-brain stereotactic coordinates. Exclusion criteria met: E10 (non-FDG PET tracer) and E6 (only ROI analyses/no whole-brain coordinate results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (bvFTD patients included), I5 (bvFTD n=9 and controls n=32, both ≥6), I6 (reports group-level bvFTD vs control comparisons), and I7 (bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) and I8 (no whole-brain coordinate-based results reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=30) and healthy controls (n=25), meeting modality and sample-size criteria. However, the paper does not report a group-level voxelwise contrast directly comparing bvFTD versus healthy controls (e.g., bvFTD < controls). The neuroimaging results are presented as correlations between gray matter and behavioral/physiological measures across the combined bvFTD+control sample and as lateralization indices, rather than as a direct bvFTD-versus-control group comparison. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (direct group comparison) is not satisfied; consequently I8 (coordinates for a bvFTD-vs-control contrast) and I7 (sample-purity requirement for such a contrast) are not met. No exclusion criteria from the list apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET (I3); includes clinically and pathologically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4) with group sizes well above 6 and healthy control groups (I5); reports group-level, between-group analyses directly comparing bvFTD versus healthy controls (I6) with voxelwise, whole-brain pattern topographies derived in MNI space (I8). The bvFTD groups are analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups), satisfying sample purity (I7). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and presents voxelwise whole-brain results and images. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports group-wise comparisons between a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group and healthy controls. Sample sizes meet the minimums (bvFTD n=25; controls n=24). VBM analyses included bvFTD versus control t-tests and reported brain correlates (text and MNI coordinates for clusters are provided for physiological correlates and group-wise atrophy is described with supplementary tables/figures), satisfying requirement for whole-brain stereotactic reporting. The bvFTD group is analysed separately (not pooled with other patient groups). No exclusion criteria from the review (e.g., ROI-only analyses, non-empirical paper, inappropriate imaging modality, case report) are met. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and neuroimaging results) is present in the supplied content, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical study that directly compares bvFTD patients with healthy controls using whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Imaging modalities include voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and 18F-FDG PET. The bvFTD group is clinically diagnosed (probable bvFTD per Rascovsky et al. criteria) and sample sizes exceed thresholds (bvFTD n=23 before QC; MRI analysis n=21, PET analysis n=23; controls n=20 MRI, n=48 PET). The paper reports group-level contrasts of bvFTD versus healthy controls for both MRI and PET, and describes stereotactic coordinate reporting (Tables 2 and 3; MNI-to-Talairach conversion). No exclusion criteria apply (FDG tracer used; whole-brain VBM/PET voxelwise results reported; not a review; not ROI-only). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so sufficient detail is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) are met.

This study uses FDG-PET and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases but does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET modality) and I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants — two cases). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (patient-group size ≥6 — the bvFTD group has only 2 patients), I6 (reports at least one group-level bvFTD vs healthy control comparison — the paper presents single-subject SPM comparisons to a normative database rather than a group-level bvFTD versus control analysis), and I8 (reports whole-brain group-level stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control contrast — no such group-level contrast is reported). Exclusion criteria met: E11 (case series/single-subject series without an appropriate patient-group vs recruited control group for group-level analysis). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Given failure to meet minimum patient-group size and absence of required group-level bvFTD-versus-control analyses, exclude from the review.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=8) and performs group-level voxelwise SPM comparisons of bvFTD vs controls using PET-derived images, the bvFTD-vs-control comparisons reported in the paper are based on early-frame florbetapir (an amyloid tracer) ‘pseudo-FDG’ images rather than on true FDG-PET data for both groups. The review’s exclusion criterion E10 disqualifies PET studies using tracers other than FDG (e.g., 18F-florbetapir) even if whole-brain voxelwise results are reported. While real FDG-PET data were acquired, they were available only for the bvFTD patients and not for controls, so the direct group comparison relied on florbetapir-derived images. Therefore the study must be excluded under E10.

This PNAS paper includes a clearly defined bvFTD patient group (n=35) and healthy controls (n=37), uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and resting-state fMRI seed-based connectivity (meets imaging modality requirement). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD and control groups ≥6). The manuscript describes group-level imaging analyses and references patient-versus-control comparisons (SI Appendix, Fig. S3 and Table S4) and reports voxelwise results with coordinates referenced in supplementary tables; seed-based connectivity results are compared across groups using Fisher r-to-z tests. Therefore it satisfies I3 (VBM/fMRI), I4 (bvFTD sample), I5 (sample size), I6 (reports group-level bvFTD vs control comparisons), I7 (bvFTD group is reported separately, not pooled), and I8 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported with coordinates indicated in SI Appendix). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Confidence is tempered by the fact that the main VBM correlation analysis reported in the excerpt was performed in patients combined (bvFTD+AD), but the paper explicitly references patient-vs-control structural comparisons and supplementary coordinate tables; per screening instructions I judge the paper rather than the excerpt and include it.

Excluded because the study uses structural T1-weighted volumetric ROI segmentation of amygdala subnuclei (FreeSurfer/GIF), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and reports ROI-based volume comparisons rather than whole-brain voxelwise stereotactic results. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes Pick's disease pathology cases), I5 (sample sizes: 132 patients, 107 controls ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (does not report a bvFTD patient-group vs healthy-control group-level contrast), I7 (no isolated bvFTD group compared to controls), I8 (no whole-brain stereotactic coordinates reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded from this meta-analysis focused on VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET studies comparing bvFTD to controls.

This study includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (I4) and uses resting-state fMRI (I3), has sufficient sample sizes (I5), performs direct group-level bvFTD vs control comparisons (I6), and presents bvFTD as a separate group (I7). However, it does not report whole-brain voxel-wise stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) coordinate results for a bvFTD-versus-control contrast (I8 not met). Moreover, the imaging findings are based on tract-specific DTI and ROI/seed-based resting-state functional connectivity (and global GM %ICV measures), i.e. ROI/tract analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise results. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E9 (reports only seed-based FC and DTI rather than qualifying modalities like VBM or FDG-PET voxelwise). For these reasons the paper should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study uses resting-state fMRI (wavelet correlation/MST) to compare 41 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with 39 healthy controls, meeting the imaging modality (fMRI) and sample requirements. The paper performs direct group-level bvFTD vs. control comparisons using whole-brain parcellation (AAL116) with data registered to MNI152 space and reports group differences in global and regional network metrics. The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied.

This study is excluded because it does NOT meet key inclusion criteria for the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD) and I5 (bvFTD sample size ≥6). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (imaging modality—study used SPECT rCBF, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET), I6 (no group-level bvFTD versus healthy control comparison reported; analyses are within‑group correlations), I7 (bvFTD-versus-control comparison not present so sample-purity criterion cannot be satisfied), and I8 (no whole‑brain bvFTD-versus-control coordinates reported for the required contrast). No exclusion criteria (E5–E11) are triggered. Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Exclusion(s) met: E6 (study reports ROI-based structural MRI analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results/coordinates). Inclusion(s) met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (sample sizes: bvFTD N=10; healthy control N=18 for psychophysiology). Inclusion(s) NOT met: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — it used FreeSurfer ROI volumetry), I6 (no group-level imaging contrast directly comparing bvFTD vs healthy controls — imaging comparisons were bvFTD vs Alzheimer’s disease), I8 (no whole-brain stereotactic-coordinate voxelwise results reported). Because at least one inclusion criterion is not met and the imaging analysis is ROI-only (E6), this paper must be excluded from the imaging-focused meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and contrast requirements for the review. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 — the study reports regional visual ratings of prefrontal atrophy on structural MRI (region-specific scores) and does not present whole-brain voxelwise results from VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET. This is a single-patient case report of a C9orf72-related bvFTD patient who underwent FDG-PET. Exclusion criteria met: E11 (case report / single patient without a control group). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET), I4 (includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (sample size >=6 patients - NOT met), I6 (group-level bvFTD vs healthy control comparison - NOT met), I7 (bvFTD group compared alone against controls - NOT met), I8 (whole-brain stereotactic coordinates for a bvFTD-versus-control group comparison - NOT met). The study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s requirement that the patient group be clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4) nor does it present a group-level bvFTD-versus-healthy control voxelwise contrast (I6). Instead, the paper develops an atrophy-based classifier in familial FTLD mutation carriers, comparing mutation carriers with dementia (CDR-plus-NACC-FTLD ≥1) versus asymptomatic carriers/controls; patient presentations are heterogeneous and pooled across mutation types and clinical syndromes, violating SAMPLE PURITY (I7). While the study uses voxelwise structural MRI / VBM-derived W-score maps (satisfying I3) and has adequate group sizes (e.g., 56 dementia cases, 35 asymptomatic in the training set; satisfying I5), it does not specifically analyze or report a bvFTD patient group compared directly against a recruited healthy control group in stereotactic coordinates (I4, I6, I7, I8 not met). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper does not fit the bvFTD-specific meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and also reports diffusion imaging, includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample using consensus criteria (25 bvFTD patients; I4), and has adequate sample sizes for both patient (n=25) and control (n=20) groups (I5). The paper reports direct group-level comparisons between bvFTD and healthy controls (two-sample t-tests for gray matter and TBSS for FA) (I6). The bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups (pure bvFTD vs controls) (I7). Whole-brain analyses were performed in MNI space with results described and supplementary tables/figures cited (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (no review/meta-analysis, whole-brain VBM reported, not an ROI-only or DTI-only paper, empirical study with control group). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) (I3). The sample includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=28) (I4) and an age-/sex-matched healthy control group (n=19) (I5). The methods and results describe pairwise voxel-wise group comparisons (t-tests) between bvFTD and controls (bvFTD vs controls) and report brain atrophy analyses for bvFTD relative to controls, satisfying the requirement for a direct group-level bvFTD-versus-control contrast (I6). The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (not pooled with other patient groups) in these comparisons (I7). The paper states that maximum voxel coordinates are provided in stereotaxic space and describes whole-brain voxelwise results and figures/tables (coordinates reported), meeting the coordinates requirement (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not PET tracer issue, not case report, etc.). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it uses FDG-PET (I3) to examine metabolic brain changes in behavioural-variant FTD; includes a clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD sample (N=82) and matched healthy controls (N=82) (I4,I5); reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM comparisons directly contrasting bvFTD versus controls (I6) and the bvFTD group is not pooled with other diagnostic groups (I7). The paper describes whole-brain voxel-level SPM t-maps and statistical results derived in stereotactic space (SPM), satisfying the requirement for reported whole-brain results (I8). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results and discussion (fulltext appears complete). No exclusion criteria from the provided list are met. Therefore the study should be included as eligible for the meta-analysis.

The study reports multimodal neuroimaging including resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses, enrolls clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (n≈43–44) and healthy controls (n≈60), and performs direct group-level comparisons between bvFTD and controls. The bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups. The paper describes whole-brain VBM results (voxelwise group comparisons), which satisfy the requirement for reporting whole-brain stereotactic results (coordinates are described as part of the VBM analysis and likely reported in the full paper/supplement). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a small-case longitudinal structural MRI study (SIENA/SIENAX) reporting one bvFTD patient, one AD patient, and five controls. It does include a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient (I4) and the bvFTD data are not pooled with other patient groups (I7). However it fails multiple required inclusion criteria: imaging modality is structural volumetry (SIENA/SIENAX), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met); the bvFTD patient group contains only a single participant (I5 not met; required >=6); and there is no group-level bvFTD-versus-control analysis (only single-case comparisons), so it does not meet the CONTRAST requirement (I6 not met). Also, no whole-brain stereotactic coordinate-based voxelwise results are reported (I8 not met). No exclusion criteria from the provided list are directly met (exclusion_criteria_applied=[]). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded because several mandatory inclusion criteria are not satisfied.

This is a single-patient case report of childhood-onset cerebellar ataxia due to a homozygous SQSTM1 mutation, not a study of behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). It does not use the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET)—only clinical MRI is reported. There is no patient group (n=1) and no healthy control group or any group-level bvFTD vs. control contrast. Therefore it fails all relevant inclusion criteria and meets the case-report exclusion criterion.

This is an empirical VBM study that directly compares a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=19) to healthy controls (n=25). Full text includes introduction, methods (including VBM and MNI registration), results (group contrasts and correlations), and discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This study is a single-patient case report (one subject) and thus does not meet key inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis. Exclusion: E11 (case report/case series). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (the study used 18F-FDG PET). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (sample size <6; only one patient), I6 (no group-level bvFTD versus healthy control comparison reported), I7 (no bvFTD group compared against controls — sample is a single subject and not pooled as a bvFTD group), and I8 (no whole-brain group-level stereotactic coordinate results reported). This study is excluded because it does not meet the review inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (contains one clinically diagnosed bvFTD participant). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is 123I-FP-CIT SPECT, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I5 (bvFTD patient group has only 1 participant, fewer than the required ≥6), I6 (no group-level comparison directly contrasting a bvFTD patient group against a healthy control group), I7 (bvFTD is pooled among multiple diagnostic groups and not analyzed as a bvFTD-only versus controls comparison), I8 (no whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control stereotactic-coordinate results reported for a bvFTD group). This is a longitudinal neuropsychological study that does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET as the primary imaging modality, and it does not report any group-level whole-brain imaging comparisons (bvFTD vs. healthy controls) with stereotactic coordinates. Although a subset underwent 11C-PiB PET (an amyloid tracer), this does not satisfy the inclusion imaging-modality criterion (I3) and PiB is an excluded tracer for PET-based inclusion. Therefore the study fails key inclusion criteria for the imaging meta-analysis.
